articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts and New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown shared an embrace at a joint practice after being urged to publicly reunite, according to Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer.

McLane reported "both teams had wanted a made-for-the-cameras reconciliation and Brown... agreed when an intermediary intervened."

94 WIP's Eliot Shorr-Parks shared a video Aug. 20 of Brown and Hurts sharing a hug and a conversation following a joint Eagles-Patriots practice.

According to McLane, the two "asked about each other's families, wished the other good luck in the coming season, and exchanged a few jokes, according to a source briefed on the interaction."

Hurts and Brown played six seasons and won Super Bowl LIX together before Brown was traded to the Patriots in June.

Brown said in a June interview with Maria Taylor he and Hurts were "not as close as we once were" but there was "still a lot of love" between them.

"I didn't truly understand why our friendship became the center of everybody's attention when it came to football because, looking back on it, we haven't been as close as we were a couple years now," Brown said.

Hurts, when asked in a recent interview with GQ's Zach Baron if he had grown apart from Brown, answered, "I mean, clearly."

The former Eagles teammates are not set to reunite this regular season. Brown is set to make his Patriots debut next Wednesday against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, while the Eagles are preparing to open the campaign the following Sunday against the visiting Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Shilo Sanders’ $11.89 million bankruptcy trial takes shocking turn as John Darjean collapses after hours of testimony
articles.summary: NFL News: John Darjean, the former school security guard seeking to keep an $11.89 million judgment against Shilo Sanders, collapsed in a Denver courtroom on Th.
articles.body: John Darjean, the former school security guard seeking to keep an $11.89 million judgment against Shilo Sanders, collapsed in a Denver courtroom on Thursday, September 3, after more than two hours of testimony. Darjean was taken to a hospital by ambulance and was released later that day, according to USA TODAY Sports. He did not return to court. The incident happened on Day 4 of Sanders’ bankruptcy trial, which is focused on whether the debt can be wiped out under Chapter 7 bankruptcy.Shilo Sanders bankruptcy trial focuses on the 2015 school incidentThe case goes back to September 17, 2015, when Sanders was 15 and attending Focus Learning Academy in Dallas, Texas. Darjean was working as a school security guard and became involved after Sanders was removed from class for breaking school rules.Darjean has said Deion Sanders asked him to take Shilo’s phone. According to Darjean, Shilo became angry when he approached him and hit him with an elbow around the neck and chest area before punching him near the face. Darjean has said the incident caused serious damage to his neck and led to years of medical problems.Shilo Sanders has given a very different version. He has denied attacking Darjean and said he was trying to get away after Darjean grabbed and choked him. Sanders has said he blacked out during the struggle and had marks on his arms and neck afterward. He has continued to argue that he was defending himself.Police records from 2015 described the incident as an assault involving serious bodily injury, with Sanders listed as the suspect. Several school witnesses have also given accounts that support Darjean’s version. At the same time, Sanders’ side has presented testimony supporting his claim that Darjean was the aggressor.The dispute later moved to Texas state court. Darjean sued Sanders in 2016, and the case eventually went to trial in 2022. Sanders did not appear at that trial after dismissing his lawyers. A Dallas County judge then awarded Darjean $11,890,937.Shilo Sanders fights to erase the $11.89 million judgmentAfter Darjean began trying to collect the money, Shilo Sanders filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in Colorado in October 2023. The current case is not about deciding the original amount of the judgment. The bankruptcy court has already ruled that the Texas judgment establishes the cause of the injuries and the damages.Instead, Judge Michael E. Romero must decide whether Sanders’ actions were a “willful and malicious injury” under federal bankruptcy law. If the judge finds that they were, the $11.89 million debt cannot be discharged. If Sanders’ self-defense argument succeeds on the remaining issues, the debt could be wiped out through bankruptcy.The trial has included testimony from Darjean, Sanders and other witnesses, along with police and medical records from 2015. A witness for Sanders was also questioned about a recorded call in which her earlier account appeared to differ from her testimony in court.Deion Sanders had been expected to remain available for possible testimony, but Judge Romero released him from that requirement after deciding his testimony was not needed.The trial was scheduled to run through Friday, September 4. articles.title: Aaron Donald's Status for Rams vs. 49ers Updated by Sean McVay Ahead of NFL Opener
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is leaving Aaron Donald's status for Week 1 up in the air.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay is leaving Aaron Donald's status for Week 1 up in the air.

McVay told reporters that the upcoming week would be a "big week" for Donald as he assesses "how he feels."

"If he feels good enough to go, great," McVay said of the defensive tackle. "If not, I've got a lot of confidence in the other guys that'll be ready to step up if that's the case, that have really gotten all the reps anyways."

The Rams open the season against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday in Melbourne, so the clock is ticking to make a decision about Donald's status. ESPN's Dan Graziano reported earlier this week that the star playing in Week 1 might be a long shot, but added that it's "still on the table."

"I would say based on everything I've been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1," Graziano reported during a Tuesday appearance on NFL Live

McVay also emphasised last week that the team isn't rushing Donald back to the field and feels confident against the 49ers with or without him.

"What I think is really good for us is if he's able to go, great. If not, that's kind of how we've been operating as is," McVay told reporters . "And guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. And so, if he's not ready and that's not what's best for him and for the team, absolutely wouldn't have him playing Australia unnecessarily."

Even though Donald didn't join the Rams until late in training camp, he's managed to get back into football shape. ESPN's Sarah Barshop reported last week that after the Rams traded for Myles Garrett, Donald began putting himself through a "very strict, regimented process that was similar to what he did when he played," so he should be pretty warmed up at this point.

Donald also isn't expected to take on a strenuous workload, as Albert Breer of SI.com reported this week that he could play between 30 and 40 snaps per game.

Even if Donald isn't expected to take on the bulk of the defensive snaps, the Rams are surely being cautious with the 35-year-old. If he isn't 100 percent ready to go by Thursday, it sounds like he'll wait to make his season debut.

According to famed sports agent Leigh Steinberg, it's because the Rams do a great job with "caponomics." The Rams did it by "creating cap room, redoing someone else's contract so that there's less salary involved and by giving that player a bonus," Steinberg told OutKick in a recent interview. "If a team is creative, they can move other contracts around and create cap space." Despite handing out all of those massive deals, the Rams were still able to sign Donald to a one-year, $20 million deal, despite being up against the salary cap. So how, exactly, are the Rams making it work? Exactly as Steinberg said: by being creative. For Stafford’s deal, the Rams have pushed his contract further into the future, spreading out the cap hit using void years, meaning Stafford’s contract will count against the salary cap in even though he won’t be on the team. Garrett’s contract is structured similarly to both Stafford’s and McDuffie’s, with a lower cap hit in the first year and larger hits later in the deal while also using void years. The reigning Defensive Player of the Year’s contract runs through 2030, but his cap hits are spread through 2034. Here are his cap hits each year through 2034: $8.4 million, $15 million, $27.57 million, $39.875 million, $48.17 million, $17.523 million, $11.5 million, $7.6 million and finally $3.3 million. To fit Aaron Donald into their group of superstars, the Rams have pushed a lot of money into the future to make it work in the present. The synergistic effect of this is that an opposing offense can't double team both Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. So somewhere in there you're going to have this spectacularly dominant player on the loose." Steinberg is also certain that Donald, who made the Pro Bowl in each of his 10 seasons in the NFL, would not have returned unless he felt he could play at an elite level. "I am sure that Aaron Donald would not have come back except that he thought he could be dominant once again," Steinberg said. "I'm assuming that time takes its toll. Being outside of football takes its toll, but it won't take too long for Aaron Donald to be back in form. No other team has two players like this backed up by another three." In addition to having Donald and Garrett, the Rams’ defensive line was already strong with Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Byron Young and Poona Ford. Steinberg said the Rams’ defensive line could be one of the best of all time, comparing it to the legendary line the Baltimore Colts had in the 1960s. "I think the only thing that would be equivalent was the Fearsome Foursome that had Merlin Olsen and Deacon Jones and Rosie Greer. The Fearsome Foursome is back and as you said, they've got Poona Ford and Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske and Byron Young and they're loaded with gifted players," Steinberg said. CAM SKATTEBO CONSIDERED RETIREMENT AFTER SEASON-ENDING ANKLE INJURY IN GIANTS ROOKIE YEAR "The Rams do a better job of scouting players, drafting players, and then finding that one superstar that can be plugged into an already dominating defense or offense." A front comparable to the Fearsome Foursome of Olsen, Jones, Greer and Lamar Lundy would give the Rams an excellent chance of getting to the Super Bowl and winning it all. Steinberg, who was inducted into the California Sports Hall of Fame in 2017, has had many high-profile clients. Across football and baseball, Steinberg’s clients include Steve Bartkowski, Steve Young, Troy Aikman, Warren Moon, Bruce Smith, Thurman Thomas, Kordell Stewart, Jeff George, Ben Roethlisberger, Myron Rolle, Matt Leinart, Mark Brunell, Ricky Williams, Howie Long, Eric Karros and Dusty Baker, among others. Steinberg was not surprised that Donald came out of retirement because so many of his clients wanted to as well. "I had 64 first-round draft picks, 12 of the players in the Hall of Fame, and when they retired, they did it with class and dignity. But then a couple weeks later, the phone would ring and the player would say, ‘Do you think there's any spot for me? Do you think I can come back?’" Steinberg said. They have structure. They miss the camaraderie in the locker room with the band of brothers that are around them," Steinberg said. "They miss the electric excitement of performing in front of packed crowds and or many of them from Pop Warner on this is all they've known and so, like the moth to the flame, professional sports is so intoxicating that players never really want to retire." They’re not going to be allowed to hide and pretend that this did not happen because it did happen.”To make matters worse, just in July 2026, two other women suffered brain injuries as they went on the X2 rollercoaster.Both the women remain under treatment as the infamous X2 ride has been temporarily closed down.How much did Travis Kelce invest in Six Flags Entertainment?Travis Kelce joined Six Flags Entertainment last year as a brand ambassador and also an investor.But that’s not all; the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player also teamed up with activist hedge fund JANA Partners to acquire a 9% stake in Six Flags Entertainment. The episode focused on the 2026 NFL season and included Matthews discussing the league and making predictions for the year.Those appearances make the sudden change shown in the alleged photos harder to accept as proof of surgery. The streaming service announced that the six-time Pro Bowl linebacker would join Michael Irvin and Nick Foles as part of the studio team for the NFL’s first regular-season game in Australia.For now, there is no reliable confirmation that Clay Matthews had plastic surgery. articles.title: Chiefs' billionaire heiress Gracie Hunt refuses to follow the family script as she builds her own empire
articles.summary: NFL News: Being born into NFL royalty can open almost every door, but it can also make it difficult to prove that you belong in the room for your own reasons. G.
articles.body: Being born into NFL royalty can open almost every door, but it can also make it difficult to prove that you belong in the room for your own reasons. Gracie Hunt knows that tension well. As the daughter of Kansas City Chiefs chairman and CEO Clark Hunt and granddaughter of franchise founder Lamar Hunt, football has always surrounded her. Yet her ambitions have grown far beyond the family business.Gracie Hunt is carving out her own identity beyond the ChiefsHunt could easily have made the Chiefs her entire professional world. Instead, she has built a portfolio that reflects interests she developed long before stepping into the family spotlight.Her journey began with soccer. As a child, she dreamed of following in the footsteps of Mia Hamm and even played the sport through high school. Her family connection to soccer ran deep, too, with her grandfather playing a role in bringing Major League Soccer to the United States.That dream changed after she suffered several concussions. Rather than allowing the setback to define her, Hunt found another competitive outlet in pageantry. She eventually won Miss Kansas USA in 2021, following an example set by her mother, Tavia Hunt, who won the same title in 1993.Her career since then has blended sports, fashion, philanthropy and advocacy. She has worked with the Chiefs Women’s Organization, supported community initiatives and explored opportunities that exist outside the football franchise."The things that have been really important to me my whole life have been faith, family, football and philanthropy," Gracie says. "Because I've always been raised with the mantra that, 'To whom much is given, much is expected'."That philosophy has helped shape the way she views her position. For Hunt, having access to the Chiefs is not necessarily a reason to claim ownership of its spotlight."When it comes to the Chiefs, there's no 'I' in 'team'. It's not about me," Gracie makes clear.Gracie Hunt’s fashion and philanthropy ventures stand on their ownOne of Hunt’s clearest efforts to establish an independent identity came through fashion. Her collaboration with broadcaster Erin Andrews gave her an opportunity to create something that was not simply connected to the Chiefs or her family."Coming out with a capsule collection with Erin was a way for me to create something that is my own," Gracie says.She explained why that distinction mattered."Obviously it's in partnership with Wear, so it's our own — but it wasn't a Chiefs project or a family initiative," she says. "It was a Gracie Hunt initiative and something that I cared about, that I spent a lot of time creating and hoping that women would love as much as I did."Her work with the Chiefs community remains important, especially the charitable efforts she experienced alongside her mother. From supporting people facing homelessness and hunger to helping build homes with Habitat for Humanity, Hunt has treated philanthropy as more than a public title.She also champions the growing influence of women in NFL fashion, pointing to designers and Chiefs WAGs who are expanding the options available to female fans.That balance may be the most interesting part of Hunt’s story. She has no need to reject her family legacy to establish herself. Instead, she is using the opportunities around her while building a career that carries her own name."I am certainly so fulfilled by all the things that I have created for myself opportunity-wise outside of football. But it's been a pleasure to be of some part of something that's greater than myself, to serve where there's room and need and to be their number one fan," she says of the Kansas City Chiefs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Former Cowboys Running Back Emmitt Smith is Sued by Investor Over Wind Farm Project
articles.summary: NFL career rushing leader Emmitt Smith is being sued by a Native American investment company over claims that the former Dallas Cowboys running back and his business partners misappropriated a $2.5 million loan that was supposed to fund a wind farm project in Texas.
articles.body:
NFL career rushing leader Emmitt Smith is being sued by a Native American investment company over claims that the former Dallas Cowboys running back and his business partners misappropriated a $2.5 million loan that was supposed to fund a wind farm project in Texas.

Kituwah LLC claimed in a lawsuit filed this week in Delaware that 4 13 Solutions used the money to repay an investor from previous dealings with Smith's company. Kituwah seeks to invest in business opportunities for the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians.

Kituwah's attorneys said Smith and the Pro Football Hall of Famer's longtime business partner, David Mosley, misrepresented their efforts to secure a U.S. Department of Energy loan that would have triggered repayment to Kituwah.

Kituwah claims the loan has accrued about $600,000 in interest and is asking a jury to determine damages. A message sent to 4 13 Solutions wasn't immediately returned. There was no information on an attorney for Smith or his company in the filing.

According to the lawsuit, Darrel Wilson of Wilson Holdings of North America LLC told Kituwah that he accepted a $2.5 million payment from Smith's company and said he didn't know what triggered the payment. Kituwah's attorneys said it was, "Essentially, like a ponzi scheme."

Kituwah claims Wilson Holdings was supposed to be repaid only after the wind farm project between Austin and San Antonio, called Project Exodus, secured permanent financing.

"Smith and Mosley knew this was improper," the lawsuit said. "Instead of telling the truth, they represented to Kituwah that 4 13 Solutions had used the money to acquire Project Exodus as promised, but that the acquisition had been held up for one reason or another."

The lawsuit claims Smith and his partners never met the requirements for securing government funding and repeatedly made excuses for why the project wasn't proceeding or stopped responding to requests.

Kituwah said it delivered the funds on Sept. 1, 2023, with the expectation of being paid back within months. The lawsuit said 4 13 Solutions promised the wind farm would be operational by December 2024, but Kituwah had seen no evidence the project even existed just a month before that date.

Kituwah said Smith and his partners claimed the wind farm project was valued at $396 million and would generate nearly $14 million in net income in its first year.

The 57-year-old Smith spent the first 13 of his 15 seasons with the Cowboys, won three championships and was the MVP of Super Bowl 28. He broke Walter Payton's rushing record in 2002 and finished with 18,355 yards.

articles.title: Cam Skattebo Reveals Giants Usage for 2026 NFL Season After Injury, Fantasy Impact and Draft Advice
articles.summary: Cam Skattebo is coming off a brutal injury during his rookie season, but the New York Giants running back is ready to take on a major workload this season.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo is coming off a brutal injury during his rookie season, but the New York Giants running back is ready to take on a major workload this season.

Skattebo said that Giants head coach John Harbaugh asked if he's willing to take 20-plus carries a game, and he said he feels ready for it.

"I had a couple talks with him letting him know, hey, I'm gonna be ready to go. And he trusted me, and he trusted the fact that I'm ready to go," Skattebo said on Sports Seriously (3:00 mark). "He got a little snippet of it in our first preseason game, and he's gonna get a big snippet on Sunday Night Football. So I'm excited to show him what I have, and we talk a lot, but when he walks up to me and tells me, 'Are you ready for 20-plus carries a game?' I think I'm in a pretty good spot."

Skattebo's rookie season ended in Week 8 when he suffered a dislocated ankle, fractured fibula and a ruptured deltoid ligament against the Philadelphia Eagles. He had put together a solid season up to that point, recording 405 rushing yards, 207 receiving yards and seven total touchdowns.

His recovery from the injury wasn't easy, and he even said he considered retiring in the weeks after.

"Yeah, definitely," Skattebo said on Up & Adams . "I would say probably a month in, like the first month, I was like, 'Damn, do I really wanna do this?' And then, it was seven games. I was like, 'I gotta go back and play.' There's no shot. If it was the end of the year and I was like, 'Okay, I'm over this.' I didn't feel that way at all. ... I think that gave me an extra step of finding that deep place and coming out of a hole that I didn't know I could come out of."

Luckily for Giants fans, Skattebo stuck with his recovery and will be back for another year. Based on his recent comments, it sounds like he could be in for a big second season.

Skattebo will be competing with Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary for touches, but if Harbaugh asked him to take 20 touches per game, it seems he'll be a focal point of the offense.

That, of course, has fantasy implications. Skattebo likely won't be anyone's first running back selection, but if Harbaugh plans to use him often, he could be a reliable second option or a flex option.

Skattebo also excels through the air, making him a great choice for PPR leagues.

articles.title: Inspiring story on women sports: "No better place to celebrate women than a stadium built for women!"- How Brittany Mahomes is turning women’s sports into a power move
articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes has never viewed women’s sports as something that simply needs support from the sidelines. For her, the real opportunity lies in buil.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes has never viewed women’s sports as something that simply needs support from the sidelines. For her, the real opportunity lies in building, owning and changing the systems around them. That message took center stage at CPKC Stadium, where Mahomes accepted a major honor and offered a powerful vision for what women’s leadership could look like for the next generation.Brittany Mahomes receives the Champions for Change AwardMahomes was named the inaugural recipient of United WE’s Champions for Change Award during a celebration marking the organization’s 35 years of advancing women’s economic and civic leadership.The setting could hardly have been more fitting.CPKC Stadium is the home of the Kansas City Current and was built specifically for a women’s professional sports team. Its existence represents a major shift in the way women’s sports are viewed, not just as entertainment, but as a serious investment with economic and cultural value.For Mahomes, the award carried significance beyond the trophy itself. She has been closely involved in the growth of the Kansas City Current alongside her husband, Patrick Mahomes, and Angie and Chris Long.Her work has placed her at the intersection of sports, business and entrepreneurship. Yet what made her speech stand out was the way she connected those roles to something much bigger.Mahomes made her position clear when she said, “It’s the smartest play on the board.”That short statement captured the heart of her approach. Investing in women is not merely about doing what feels right. Mahomes sees it as a decision with the potential to create lasting value.Brittany Mahomes shares a powerful message about women’s sportsMahomes used the occasion to reflect on what CPKC Stadium represents.“This building alone is a powerful symbol of the incredible growth and impact our collective efforts have made for women in leadership and women’s sports.”The importance of that message goes beyond one stadium.For years, women’s professional sports have fought for greater attention, better facilities and stronger financial backing. The creation of a venue specifically designed for a women’s team offers a visible example of what can happen when investment moves from conversation to action.Mahomes also spoke about the importance of representation. She described herself as part of a generation that is beginning to experience what happens when women receive access to positions traditionally dominated by men.“I’m proud to be one of many women who represent the first generation to truly see what happens when women are given keys to the stadium and the boardroom,” she added. “We talk a lot about setting an example for the next generation, and as a mom, my goal isn’t for my daughters and my son to see women’s leadership as an inspiration. I want them to see women in positions of power and leadership as the norm. I want them to grow up in a world where women owning a team or a company is the standard.”That distinction matters.Inspiration can begin a movement, but normalization can sustain it. Mahomes wants children to grow up seeing women as owners, executives, athletes and decision-makers without treating those roles as unusual.Brittany Mahomes reveals why motherhood is not a limitationPerhaps the most personal part of Mahomes’ message came when she addressed the idea of balancing motherhood with ambition.Rather than describing motherhood as another responsibility that women must somehow fit around their careers, she presented it as a source of strength.“And I want them to know that being a mother and an athlete, an entrepreneur, or whatever they want to be, isn’t just a balancing act. It is a power move.”The line carries particular weight because Mahomes herself has built a public identity across several worlds.She has been an athlete, businesswoman, investor and mother while remaining deeply involved in professional sports. Her experience gives the statement a personal edge. She is not simply talking about an abstract idea of women having multiple roles. She is speaking about the possibility of embracing those roles without allowing one to erase the others.That perspective also challenges an old expectation placed on women. Success does not have to come with a choice between family and professional ambition.For Mahomes, the goal is to make room for both.Brittany Mahomes shares emotional Instagram post after the honorFollowing the event, Mahomes also took to Instagram to share her reaction to the recognition and the significance of the venue.In the post, she celebrated United WE, the award and the broader meaning of CPKC Stadium. Her message offered a more personal look at what the morning meant to her.Mahomes wrote:“Such an inspiring morning with @unitedwe__ celebrating progress and influencing action! It was such an honor to receive the inaugural Champion for Change award in the stadium that represents what it looks like when women’s needs are prioritized in sports and in the workplace. No better place to celebrate women than a stadium built for women!Thank you @unitedwe__ and @wendydoyle for the incredible honor!”The Instagram message echoed the theme of her speech. She was celebrating more than an individual achievement. The post placed the spotlight on the larger movement around women’s sports and workplaces where women have greater opportunities to lead.Her reference to women’s needs being prioritized is especially significant. CPKC Stadium is not just a physical building. It has become a symbol of what dedicated investment can create when women’s sports are treated as worthy of purpose-built spaces and serious resources.Mahomes later reinforced that larger ambition during her speech.“We are here to build real equity and create spaces where women don’t just have a seat at the table, but they own the building that the table sits in,” she said.That is perhaps the clearest picture of the future Mahomes wants to help build.The conversation is no longer only about giving women an opportunity to participate. It is about giving them the power to shape the organizations, businesses and sports leagues in which they participate.And that makes her Champions for Change recognition more than another accolade. It reflects a growing shift in women’s sports, where athletes, investors, owners and business leaders are increasingly becoming architects of the future.For Mahomes, the message is simple. Women should not have to wait for a seat to be offered. They should have the opportunity to own the table, the room and, in her memorable words, the building around it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body:
If there's one thing you can count on happening for the Kansas City Chiefs this season, it's center Creed Humphrey being great.

A second-round draft pick in 2021, Humphrey was great right off the jump. He has been the heart and soul of the Chiefs' offensive line, helping them win back-to-back Super Bowls. Humphrey is a three-time All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler.

Kansas City Chiefs C Creed Humphrey May Have Most Valuable Odds to Win NFL Protector of the Year in 2026

Iain MacMillan of Sports Illustrated recently examined the odds from FanDuel for NFL Protector of the Year in 2026. The sportsbook currently has Humphrey at +1500, the sixth-highest odds among all offensive linemen. MacMillan believes given those odds and Humphrey's skills, that is a great bet to make.

"That leads me to Creed Humphrey, the center for the Kansas City Chiefs. He has long been looked at as one of the best centers in the NFL, and he was named a finalist for the award last season. If the Chiefs bounce back in 2026 and return to the playoffs, and if Humphrey's play at center ends up being a pivotal factor in that, I could see the voters giving him the nod."

Barring injury, it's hard to imagine Humphrey not being a finalist for the award again this year. If the Chiefs revitalize their rushing attack with Kenneth Walker III pounding the rock, that will help Humphrey's chances all the more. Winning Protector of the Year would pretty much complete Humphrey's already Hall of Fame-worthy resume.

Chiefs' Interior OL Could Be Best in the NFL

We know how great Humphrey is, and next to him is two-time Pro Bowl right guard Trey Smith . Humphrey and Smith entered the NFL together, and were given big-time contract extensions by the Chiefs.

Over at left guard is third-year man Kingsley Suamataia. After not fitting in as an offensive tackle during his rookie season, he found his niche at guard. Suamataia improved steadily throughout 2025, and could be poised to join Humphrey and Smith as a Pro Bowler this season. The Chiefs also have nice depth behind those three in center Hunter Nourzad, as well as guards Mike Caliendo and Joshua Ezeudu.

articles.title: ‘This isn’t good’: Buffalo Bills turf raises concerns before season opener
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills are playing in a brand-new stadium this year. While that should be a reason for excitement and something both the team and its fans can loo...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills are playing in a brand-new stadium this year. While that should be a reason for excitement and something both the team and its fans can look forward to ahead of opening day, the new venue has already come with its fair share of issues.

Over the last several weeks, the Bills have faced criticism over hundreds, and potentially thousands, of seats that feature obstructed views. Now, the team has another issue to deal with: the playing surface.

After enduring negative headlines and criticism from fans over the seats with obstructed views , the Bills are now dealing with another embarrassing issue as the grass field at their brand-new $2.2 billion stadium has begun falling apart.

Following only two preseason games, the Bills removed the entire grass field that had been installed in October 2025. The grass roots, however, apparently failed to properly take hold, with large sections of sod repeatedly being torn up by players during the two preseason contests and two open practices at the stadium.

In an article published by The Athletic this week, several experts expressed concerns about the condition of the field.

"I saw their press release and heard some of their rationale, and they probably ought to start their stories 'Once upon a time,'" said an award-winning sports agronomist who has helped install dozens of NFL and college football fields over the decades. "That's the worst sod I've seen in the NFL in my career. I can't even imagine how that could have happened."

Although natural grass is generally considered a safer option than artificial turf, one expert does not believe that was true in this particular situation, considering the poor condition of the field.

"Yes, natural turf is safer in a perfect setting," said Tony Dick, a sports management professor at Baldwin Wallace University and former Cleveland Browns assistant head groundskeeper. "But if you have the situation like you have in Buffalo — and I went back and watched the film — you cannot tell me that field was safer than the artificial turf they just left.

"I'm never putting Josh Allen on a field in that condition," he continued.

With the grass already coming apart just weeks ahead of the NFL season, the Bills are now working against the clock to get new sod installed. The team's season-opening matchup with the Detroit Lions on "Thursday Night Football" is only two weeks away, and that game will begin a stretch of three consecutive contests at the new Highmark Stadium over just 18 days.

The experts who spoke with The Athletic expect the replacement turf to be ready and capable of holding up for the season opener against the Lions, but what happens beyond that is much less certain.

"They will have a difficult time," the anonymous agronomist said. "There's so much going wrong, and there's so little time. If that field makes it through the second game, I'll be shocked."

Dick, meanwhile, believes the Bills could ultimately be forced to abandon the natural grass field altogether.

"You might have artificial turf back in there within three years," Dick said. "Just because it's safer than whatever that was."

Needless to say, the concern from experts has led to concerns from the sports world.

"OK, I said it looks cool as hell but you can't have *this*, either. I'll never accept that there's just no solution. I can see all the soccer pitches in Europe from my back yard," wrote soccer commentator Ryan Burns .

"I'm sticking to my completely fabricated theory that the stadium is cursed. Mainly because I have way too much free time," wrote sportswriter Rhys Scott .

"Owners hesitant to switch to natural grass likely are monitoring this closely. Players have lobbied for natural grass, but this isn't good," wrote Mike Jones of The Athletic.

"I get the feeling Bills fans should enjoy seeing games on grass while they can. Seems like the possibility of going back to artificial turf is very real in the next couple years. Makes no sense, if Green Bay can manage, Buffalo should too," wrote football commentator Helmet Addict .

"Cursed franchise," wrote prominent Kansas City Chiefs content creator Clay Wendler .

It will certainly be interesting to see how the turf holds up this season.

articles.title: “One of the best things that happened for Travis”: Jason Kelce opens up on Travis Kelce’s lowest moment and why getting kicked off Cincinnati made him stronger
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce’s path to becoming one of the NFL’s biggest stars did not begin with a smooth rise through college football. Before the Super Bowl wins, .
articles.body: Travis Kelce’s path to becoming one of the NFL’s biggest stars did not begin with a smooth rise through college football. Before the Super Bowl wins, Pro Bowls and record-setting seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs, Kelce had to fight his way back from a painful setback at Cincinnati, and Jason Kelce now believes that difficult period helped shape the player his younger brother eventually became.Jason revisited that chapter while speaking with former NFL tight end Greg Olsen on the latest episode of Youth Inc. podcast, where the brothers’ different paths to NFL success came up during a discussion about young athletes dealing with adversity.Jason Kelce says getting kicked off Cincinnati forced Travis Kelce to growJason Kelce did not describe Travis’ Cincinnati experience as something that simply damaged his career. Instead, he looked back at it as the kind of setback that forced his younger brother to understand what he wanted and how hard he needed to work for it.Travis arrived at Cincinnati with a scholarship, but he was not considered a major national recruit. He also dealt with injuries during his college career, while his role on the field remained limited early on. During his freshman season in 2009, he recorded just one reception for three yards as Cincinnati went 12-1 and reached the Sugar Bowl.The bigger blow came before the 2010 season, when Cincinnati dismissed Travis after he failed a drug test. The decision cost him his scholarship and kept him away from the team for an entire season, leaving the future Chiefs tight end with no clear path back into college football.Jason explained why he now views that moment differently while speaking on Youth Inc. with Greg Olsen.“I think one of the best things that happened for Travis was to get suspended for a year ... was him to get kicked off the team.”Jason also pointed to the lessons Travis had to learn while dealing with injuries and other problems, arguing that those experiences gave his brother something many young prospects never develop until much later.“I think it’s really easy sometimes to look at those things as negatives, and they are in the moment, like it sucks, but ultimately it’s only a negative if you allow it to stop you.”That mindset became important because Travis did not simply wait for another opportunity. He worked outside football, continued his studies and eventually earned a path back to Cincinnati as a walk-on. Travis Kelce turned the setback into the start of his NFL riseJason also played a major role in that comeback. Before the 2011 spring season, he spoke with Cincinnati coach Butch Jones and assistant Kerry Coombs on Travis’ behalf, asking them to give his younger brother another opportunity.When Cincinnati finally brought Travis back, he had to meet strict expectations while rebuilding his standing inside the program. He returned with something to prove, and the results soon followed as he became a much bigger part of the offense and settled into the tight end position.The transformation became especially clear in 2012, when Travis caught 45 passes for 722 yards and eight touchdowns during his senior season. That performance helped put him back on the NFL radar after his career had once looked uncertain.The Chiefs ultimately selected him No. 63 overall in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft, giving Travis the opportunity that his Cincinnati dismissal had nearly taken away.In Jason’s case, that is the part of the story that matters most. The suspension did not disappear from Travis’ past, but it became one of the experiences that pushed him to change, work and earn another chance. Years later, with Travis established as a Chiefs superstar, Jason sees that painful Cincinnati chapter as a setback that ultimately helped his brother find his way.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LSU leaves former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris off Week 1 roster despite court ruling in Tigers' favor
articles.summary: LSU reversed course, opting to leave Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris off its roster in 2026.
articles.body:
When LSU takes the field against Clemson on Saturday, former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris will not be with the team. Both players — who were subject to various legal challenges over their eligibility — were left off LSU's Week 1 roster when the team submitted it to the SEC on Friday, according to ESPN.

After various arguments and legal filings, LSU earned a major victory Thursday , as a judge ruled in favor of Harris and Wright against the SEC. In doing so, the judge paved the way for LSU to include both players on its 2026 roster, even though that would go against the SEC's wishes.

But despite that court ruling, LSU ultimately decided not to risk the ire of the SEC or other conference members, leaving Harris and Wright off the roster. For now. The players can still be added to the roster at any point during the season since they are already enrolled at the university. LSU has two open roster spots.

Both players have experience in the NFL, as Harris signed with the New Orleans Saints in May, and Wright saw time with the Philadelphia Eagles and the Cleveland Browns before they were cut and signed with LSU.

A lawsuit — filed by the SEC against LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin on Thursday — may have influenced the school's decision. In it, the conference argued both LSU and Kiffin "waged a deliberate and coordinated campaign to recruit professional athletes to play football for LSU during the 2026-27 season, including players who had signed NFL contracts with the Cleveland Browns, New Orleans Saints, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers."

In the lawsuit, the SEC asked to be allowed to enforce its First Amendment rights to tell members to comply with its rules. In an attempt to prevent players with professional experience returning to college, the SEC and various other conferences adopted a policy in August that would ban the practice.

But, crucially, that policy did not apply to Harris and Wright, who had already received a temporary-restraining order from a judge, allowing them to return to college in 2026. In the aftermath of the SEC's attempt to ban the tactic, Kiffin initially said LSU would comply with that ruling . But as it became clear Harris' and Wright's situation was not as clear cut, Kiffin said he would wait and see how Thursday's ruling turned out before making a call.

That decision opened the door for Kiffin to add both Harris and Wright to LSU's roster Friday night if the school wanted to test the conference.

While it seemed like Kiffin wanted both players on his roster during the legal process, he (or LSU) apparently decided it wasn't smart to go against the SEC at the last second given everything that has unfolded this week.

As part of Thursday's ruling, the judge " enjoined LSU from taking action to prevent the players from competing ," per Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger. Leaving Harris and Wright off the roster could lead to future legal battles if their absence continues for weeks.

Had Harris and Wright been put on LSU's roster, the school would have potentially faced retaliation — or more legal challenges — from the SEC or its members, which were reportedly furious over LSU's attempt to use pro players.

articles.title: Jayden Daniels Fantasy Prediction 2026: Only Worth It If He Falls to Round 7
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels enters his third NFL season carrying immense fantasy upside, looking to bounce back after a slew of injuries completely derailed his 2025 camp...
articles.body:
Jayden Daniels enters his third NFL season carrying immense fantasy upside, looking to bounce back after a slew of injuries completely derailed his 2025 campaign. We already know exactly what the ceiling looks like when he is fully healthy: He finished as a top-5 fantasy quarterback in 2024, and he gave us a bit of everything in the process.

Should You Draft Jayden Daniels in Fantasy Football?

Daniels' ADP is 61.2 in PFN's Free Fantasy Mock Draft Simulator . His positional rank, which is a consensus of my colleague Kyle Soppe and me, is QB4. We have him projected for 20.73 fantasy points per game, which is awesome. The question is, do we want to draft him?

Let's start with the obvious. Daniels is good at football, I like him as a player, and I do want to draft him. The problem, as always, is opportunity cost. Philosophically, I am mostly opposed to taking a quarterback anywhere early in the draft.

This season, the elite quarterbacks and even the sub-elite quarterbacks are going later than they have in previous years. But I think late-round quarterback is back, and quarterback is so deep that you can get quality QB1 or QB1-upside type quarterbacks very late, which makes it hard to take any quarterback early on.

With that said, rounds 6 and 7 are really tough this year, especially if you pick on the front end. There aren't any players I particularly like there, which makes taking a quarterback a bit more appealing. If you're in shallower formats, I endorse taking onesie positions earlier than you would in deeper leagues.

Daniels is one of only four quarterbacks since 2011 to make at least 10 starts as a rookie and average over 20 fantasy points per game. He joins a list that includes Cam Newton, Justin Herbert, and Robert Griffin III. These quarterbacks mostly went on to do good things. RG3 got hurt, but we're pretty confident he would have been a top fantasy quarterback for years to come had he not.

Daniels, of course, was a league winner as a rookie. He was a double-digit round pick, and he had a massive Week 17. I remember that because he carried me to a title. Great season. We were all happy, excited to draft him the next year. Of course, we know it didn't go as well.

He averaged 16.8 fantasy points per game last season, but it was really 18.9 points per game if you remove that Week 14 game he returned in with that dislocated elbow, which he never should have played in. That, of course, is the story of Daniels' 2025 season: injuries. He dealt with a sprained knee, a strained hamstring, and a dislocated elbow.

While the injuries are not ideal, and we know hamstrings tend to linger, by all accounts these are one-off, fluky injuries. I'm not ready to slap him with an injury-prone label. I don't believe we can predict injury anyway, and I'm not fading him for that reason.

I think the situation this year should be better. I believe in improved offensive play calling and improved offense in general, as the team now has a more confident running back room. They had a lot of injuries last year, which should help the passing game, and, of course, they have Stefon Diggs as a WR2. Daniels has not really had a true second option in the passing game aside from Terry McLaurin during his two years in the league. I think Diggs will help out a lot.

We know elite difference-making quarterbacks move the needle, and Daniels can be that. If you want to take him and he falls to that late-sixth, early-seventh-round area, I am okay with that. But as a general roster construction philosophy, I'm not really looking to take quarterbacks that early this season.

Analysis provided by PFN Analyst Kyle Soppe .

You drafted Daniels as a game-breaker and, for the record, I'm on board with that. You're going to need to stay patient.

Philadelphia's defense is tough, Dallas is improved, and the Seahawks won the Super Bowl last year because of the upside they had on that side of the ball.

That's a tough three-game run to start the season, but if Daniels is poised to be the asset that he was as a rookie, he manages the September stretch, rounds into form during the middle months, and then carries you to glory in the postseason (Falcons, Vikings, and Jaguars).

To get there, you might have to swallow an underwhelming Week 1.

He's a fringe QB1 for me this week. This is a strong defense and an offense that can control tempo. If he's struggling for quantity and quality, even the best version of him will struggle to hang 20+ fantasy points.

That said, if you believed enough in this profile to pay up for him at the draft, this matchup shouldn't have you shaking. He had a five-touchdown pass against them in December of his rookie season, and he logged 6+ rush attempts in every meeting with the divisional rival.

Daniels is on the short list of QBs I give a real chance at unseating Josh Allen atop the QB position. If we see a healthy version of him threatening this dangerous defense in a variety of ways, I think you're thrilled with your decision to draft him, even if the Week 1 point total isn't eye-popping.

Where Daniels Ranks Among 2026 Quarterbacks

articles.title: Why Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris are at the center of college football's biggest controversy
articles.summary: Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris are at the center of college football's biggest controversy after going from the NFL to LSU. Here's more on them:
articles.body:
Last season, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris were starters on an Ole Miss football team that was a few plays away from making the national championship game. Outside of their own state, though, they were relatively anonymous.

Over the past several weeks, that's changed dramatically.

Wright and Harris are at the center of the most intense and breathlessly debated story in college sports as the two former Ole Miss players are set to return to college to play for Lane Kiffin at LSU , even after they had both previously signed NFL contracts.

Both players were members of the 2022 recruiting class who thought they had exhausted their college eligibility last season, but after the NCAA adopted a five-for-five eligibility model in June that would have given them another season of eligibility had outgoing seniors been grandfathered in with the new rule, they took their case to court and were granted a temporary restraining order that will allow them to compete during the 2026 season. Their effort to return to college received another boost on Thursday, Sept. 3, when a Louisiana judge granted an injunction that would prohibit the SEC or NCAA from punishing any school that puts former professional players on the field.

Where do things stand with Wright and Harris? And how, exactly, did we get to this point?

While they weren't as widely known as some of their teammates, stars like quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy, Wright and Harris were consistently productive players for an Ole Miss team in 2025 that won a school-record 13 games and made the semifinals of the College Football Playoff, where it narrowly lost to Miami.

After the season, Wright and Harris, both of whom were seniors, weren't selected in the 2026 NFL Draft. Both, however, signed professional contracts. Wright agreed to a deal with the Philadelphia Eagles, who waived him on Aug. 10. One day later, he was claimed off waivers by the Cleveland Browns and suited up for the team in its preseason game against the Buffalo Bills on Aug. 22. He was waived two days later. Harris, meanwhile, signed with the New Orleans Saints before being waived on Aug. 10.

Even as both players were trying to make an NFL roster, they were part of a group of athletes from the 2022 recruiting class that had brought forth a lawsuit against the NCAA for an additional year of eligibility. A judge in Louisiana granted them a temporary restraining order and opened their path back to college. Both Wright and Harris committed to LSU, where they reunited with Kiffin, who had left Ole Miss for the Tigers after the 2025 regular season. Harris said on Friday, Sept. 4 that he was originally planning on returning to the Rebels, but that the coaching staff wanted to move him from defensive tackle to the offensive line.

In response to those moves, the SEC passed a measure that would ban NFL players from returning to college and competing for any of the conference's 16 members. But on Thursday, Sept. 3, two days before LSU's season-opener against Clemson, Judge William Jorden approved a preliminary injunction that prohibits the SEC and NCAA from punishing a school like LSU that would put former NFL players on the field.

Will Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris play for LSU?

Thanks to Thursday's ruling from Jorden, the door is open for Wright and Harris to join the LSU roster.

Wright told reporters that he plans to be ready to play for the Tigers against Clemson on Saturday, Sept. 5 and added that he had practiced with LSU for two days this week.

"I've been working out doing my own thing before I was able to practice, so I'm definitely well prepared," Wright said .

Harris, meanwhile, said he will need a couple of weeks but that he will be ready for the Tigers' highly anticipated Sept. 19 game at Ole Miss, in which Kiffin will return to the school where he coached for six seasons before his messy exit last November.

Even with Jorden's ruling, though, LSU could be risking significant repercussions from the SEC. As such, they were left off LSU's roster heading into the season opener against Clemson. They could, however, join the team later as they're both enrolled with the school.

While both players will give LSU some depth, neither figures to be a starter for the Tigers, at least to start the season. Wright is a productive tight end who earned second-team All-SEC honors last season, but he figures to be behind 6-foot-7 sophomore star Trey'Dez Green, who had seven touchdown receptions last season. Harris, a 6-foot-8 defensive lineman, will likely also be coming off the bench.

Last season, Wright caught 39 passes for 635 yards and five touchdowns. As a junior in 2024, he had 27 catches for 394 yards and four touchdowns.

Wright played his first two college seasons at Virginia Tech before transferring to Ole Miss.

Harris was a part of a stout Ole Miss defense last season, totaling 58 tackles, three sacks and an interception.

The Mississippi native spent his first four college seasons with the Rebels. During that time, he put up 122 tackles, 5.5 sacks, an interception and a forced fumble.

articles.title: Projecting the Win Totals for All 32 NFL Teams
articles.summary: It's Labor Day weekend. Cookouts galore. One last trip to the public pool. And the unofficial end of summer.
articles.body:
It's Labor Day weekend. Cookouts galore. One last trip to the public pool. And the unofficial end of summer.

If summer is toast, then that means fall is here. And if fall is here, then football is here along with it.

On Wednesday, the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks will kick off the 2026 NFL season. For fans of all 32 teams (OK, more like 27 of them), it's a time of hope. Of optimism. And to varying degrees, of expectations.

Of course, whether those expectations are reasonable or not is another matter. Granted, every year teams surprise (for better or worse) just as the Patriots did in going from worst to first and a Super Bowl berth in 2025. But for every team who explodes into the playoffs or falls apart, there are two who get a little better—or a little worse.

We're going to check the temperature on those expectations here. Using the Over/Under totals at FanDuel as our thermometer, we're going to examine which teams are going to exceed expectations. Which ones will fail to meet them.

And predict all 32 teams' records while we're at it.

This is one of the easier calls to make in the entire NFL—the last time the Bills failed to hit the 11-win mark was the 10-6 record the team posted in Josh Allen's second season in 2019.

The Bills added a high-end wide receiver for Allen in D.J. Moore. James Cook is the reigning rushing champ. The Buffalo defense ranked seventh in the league last year and remains mostly intact.

As good as the Patriots were last year, the Bills should be the favorites in the AFC East.

Folks, the Miami Dolphins are a hot mess.

This is a team that purged most of its offensive talent in the offseason outside of running back De'Von Achane. A team with a quarterback in Malik Willis who showed promise in Green Bay—but was a trainwreck in Tennessee. The offense looked offensive most of the offseason.

There is some young talent on defense—but also significant issues on the defensive line and in the secondary.

When the 2027 NFL Draft kicks off in Washington next April, the Dolphins may well be on the clock.

The Patriots are the reigning AFC champions, but this relatively low win total indicates a level of skepticism that New England can repeat its 2025 success playing a first-place schedule instead of a historically easy one.

Still, the Patriots have an excellent young quarterback in Drake Maye. The offense got better at wide receiver with the acquisition of A.J. Brown. And while there are questions on the edge defensively, this is a unit that was eighth in the league in 2025.

The Pats may well regress. But they aren't going to regress that much.

It has been a while since Jets fans saw a winner—the team's last winning season came all the way back in 2015.

That depressing streak isn't going to end in 2026.

There are reasons for at least some optimism—if No. 2 overall pick David Bailey is the real deal, the New York defense should be improved. But there are just far too many questions on offense outside of wide receiver Garrett Wilson and Breece Hall.

The Geno Smith era will be short. And not fun.

Last year the Dallas Cowboys had one of the NFL's most prolific offenses—and a defense that couldn't cover a wall with paint.

That defense is going to determine how far Dallas gets in 2026.

There are new starters at all three levels, whether it's Rashan Gary up front, Dee Winters or Jaishawn Barham at linebacker or Caleb Downs and Jalen Thompson at safety.

That defense isn't going to suddenly morph into the '85 Bears. But it should be improved enough to get Dallas to 10 wins and a Wild Card spot.

On one hand, if the young talent in New York can stay healthy and takes a step forward in 2026, the Giants could be a tough out. Jaxson Dart, Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers are an exciting young trio on offense. Edge-rusher Abdul Carter came on strong late last season. Rookie linebacker Arvell Reese has the potential to be a difference-maker.

However, there is also a lot that can go wrong in the Big Apple, the team still has multiple question marks and New York has had two winning seasons over the last decade.

They won't get one this year either. But they will still clear this number—barely.

The Eagles have won the NFC East three of the last four seasons, making a pair of Super Bowl trips along the way. But the team faces more questions than usual in 2026.

With A.J. Brown now catching passes in New England, can DeVonta Smith step up and be a true "alpha" wide receiver? With edge-rusher Jonathan Greenard hurt, can youngster's like Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith anchor the Philly pass-rush?

There are viable questions as to whether the Eagles can hang with the NFC's best. But they are still the class of the division.

The Washington Commanders went from the penthouse to the outhouse in 2025, following up a trip to the NFC Championship Game with an injury-marred five-win campaign.

That the injury bug has already taken a chunk out of the team in 2026 with the loss of Pro Bowl tackle Laremy Tunsil isn't a great sign.

The Commanders made an effort to get better on both sides of the ball, whether it's the likes of running back Rachaad White and wide receiver Stefon Diggs on offense or edge-rusher Odafe Oweh and rookie linebacker Sonny Styles on defense.

But the offensive line and a shaky run game will be Washington's undoing.

The times they are-a-changing in Baltimore. After missing the playoffs last season, the ravens sent head coach John Harbaugh packing. The team also spent big for edge-rusher Trey Hendrickson to bolster a pass rush that was among the league's worst in 2025.

Jesse Minter's team is a good one. Quarterback Lamar Jackson. Running back Derrick Henry. Linebacker Roquan Smith. Safety Kyle Hamilton. All are legitimate stars. The Ravens are absolutely contenders not only in the AFC North but the conference as a whole.

But the Ravens play in one of the league's toughest divisions, and Baltimore has cleared 11 wins just twice over the last six seasons.

The Cincinnati Bengals are the Dallas Cowboys of the AFC.

Even with Joe Burrow banged up last year, the Bengals moved the ball with regularity. But the defense made tissue paper look tough, and Cincinnati missed the playoffs for the third straight year.

That defense has been overhauled, with defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence the centerpiece of a bevy of personnel moves. If the Bengals can get even average play out of that defense and the offensive line holds up, the Bengals could do more than just make the playoffs, And do more than win the AFC North.

The Bengals can make it all the way to SoFi Stadium and Super Bowl LXI.

There isn't a number on this list this writer would smash more than the "under" on Cleveland—and I say that as a lifelong Browns fan.

Yes, the Browns re-tooled an offensive line that struggled last year in the offseason. The addition of wide receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston injected some badly-needed talent into the passing attack. And even with edge-rusher Myles Garrett gone, the Browns should still field an above-average defense.

But the Browns also have arguably the worst quarterback situation in the NFL. Deshaun Watson is a has-been. Shedeur Sanders is a never-was.

And it's going to be another long season at The Factory of Sadness.

It's the start of a new era in the Steel City. And the end of an old one.

The Steelers have a new head coach for the first time in a long time, with Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin. Pittsburgh also has an old quarterback in Aaron Rodgers, who has already announced that the 2026 season will be his last.

The Steelers have veteran talent on both sides of the ball. They are the defending AFC North champions. The team hasn't had a losing record since 2003.

Is Pittsburgh a Super Bowl contender? No.

But they'll clear 7.5 wins—with relative ease.

Bold Trade Predictions Before Season Kickoff 🏈

1 Reason Why Commanders' Fans Should Be Optimistic 🙏

The Bears experienced quite a turnaround last year—after winning just five games in 2024, the Bears went 11-6 and won the NFC North in 2025.

Now, there's enthusiasm in Chicago—and expectations. Expectations that the Bears will not only make the playoffs but make a run in them. That young quarterback Caleb Williams will become a legitimate star in his third season.

The offense should be formidable. But there are questions at all three levels of the Chicago defense, especially up front. In a meat-grinder of a division, that defense is going to leave Bears fans disappointed this year.

The Lions are looking to rebound in 2026. Two years ago, the Lions won 15 games and were the NFC's No. 1 seed. Last year, the team lost three of their last four games and missed the playoff altogether.

Offensively, Detroit has an assemblage of talent that rivals any in the NFL, and the Lions have a solid veteran quarterback in Jared Goff. In players like edge-rusher Aidan Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell, there's young talent on defense.

There are potential issues in the defensive backfield, and those issues are going to cost the Lions a couple of wins this year. But the Lions will still be good enough to win the NFC North and get back into the postseason tournament.

This one will send some eyebrows skyward after the Packers made the playoffs last year, but Green Bay did so as a 9-7-1 football team that lost four in a row to close the regular season.

That slide is going to continue in 2026.

Offensively, there are major questions on the ground after veteran running back Josh Jacobs landed on the Commissioner's Exempt List. With Micah Parsons opening the season on the PUP list, Green Bay could also struggle mightily to pressure opposing quarterbacks.

It's been a while since Green Bay was a last-place team. But for the first time in the 21st century, it's going to happen in 2026.

Whether the Minnesota Vikings clear 8.5 wins and/or make the playoffs in 2026 will depend largely on one person—quarterback Kyler Murray.

Murray has an excellent trio of wide receivers at his disposal in Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings. The ground game and offensive line aren't great, but they are capable. Brian Flores runs an aggressive defense in the Twin Cities that has talent at all three levels in Dallas Turner, linebacker Blake Cashman and safety Josh Metellus.

We have seen Kevin O' Connell resurrect one quarterback's career in Sam Darnold. This year O' Connell will work his magic again with Murray and the Vikings will win 10 games.

Whether that will good enough for a playoff spot is another matter.

On one hand, the Houston Texans head into the 2026 season with one of the best defenses in the game—a unit that is loaded from front to back, including maybe the best edge-rusher duo in the league.

On the other hand, there are questions on offense. Quarterback C.J. Stroud imploded in the playoffs. There's a new lead running back in David Montgomery. And a new wide receiver in Kayshon Boutte after Jayden Higgins was lost to a torn ACL.

That defense will keep the team in games on a weekly basis. The Texans will win more games than they lose.

But Houston isn't a real Super Bowl threat.

Last year was a tale of two seasons in Indianapolis. The team got off to a white-hot start, winning eight of 10 games ahead of the bye week. But then quarterback Daniel Jones tore his Achilles, and the team didn't win another game the rest of the way.

Jones is supposed to be ready for Week 1, but he's not the only uncertainty on offense. New No. 1 wide receiver Alec Pierce missed most of the summer. Tight end Tyler Warren is banged-up.

The injuries extend to the defense—a defense that was already looking at starting two rookies in 2026.

There are just too many unanswered questions for the Colts this season. Too many things that can go wrong—especially if Jones can't recapture last year's level of play.

While the Colts were falling apart down the stretch last year, the Jaguars were doing the opposite, posting eight straight wins to close the season 13-4 and win the AFC South.

There are admittedly some reasons for concern in Duval County this year. Linebacker Devin Lloyd and running back Travis Etienne both played major roles for the team last year. Both are gone—and the team didn't make and major moves to replace them.

Trevor Lawrence is coming off the best season of his career at the helm of a loaded passing attack. Jacksonville's defense was the toughest in the league to run on last year.

Even if the Jags take a step back, they are still the class of the division.

It has been a dark time in Tennessee of late—in each of the past two years, the team has gone 3-14. Now, Robert Saleh has come to Nashville to try to reverse that futility.

How the 2026 season goes will be largely determined by Cam Ward's progress in his second professional season. The first was uneven, although there's a new No. 1 wideout in Tennessee in rookie Carnell Tate.

The Titans defense could also be an issue after ranking outside the top-20 in total defense a year ago. For all Saleh's prowess as a defensive coordinator, the personnel on that side of the ball for the Titans isn't scaring anyone.

There will be progress—but digging out of this hole will take time.

The Atlanta Falcons are headed toward a rough season.

With Michael Penix Jr. rehabbing an ACL tear, the team signed Tua Tagovailoa as a stopgap starter at quarterback. But Tagovailoa has been so God-awful this summer that now the team may have little recourse but to roll Penix out if he's anywhere close to ready.

Meanwhile, on defense the team that led the NFC in sacks last year has been devastated on the edge. James Pearce Jr. will miss the first eight games due to a personal conduct policy suspension. Jalon Walker will miss the entire season after tearing his ACL in the offseason.

Settle down—this doesn't mean the Panthers will be good.

Yes, the Panthers were the "champions" of the NFC South last year. But the team "won" the division with just eight victories—and it's hard to see where marked progress is going to come from.

Bryce Young showed some improvement under center last year, but no one's mentioning him with Josh Allen anytime soon. The passing game weapons are—OK. The ground game is a question mark—as is just about every level of the defense.

This is a mediocre team that will win ugly and hover around .500 most of the year before missing the playoffs.

The New Orleans Saints haven't won 10 games or made the postseason since 2020—the last time they won the division.

New Orleans has a good shot to knock out at least two of the three in 2026.

Quarterback Tyler Shough wasn't great as a rookie, but he got better as the season wore on. The addition of running back Travis Etienne should give the ground game a boost. The Saints also added a veteran presence in the middle of the defense in linebacker Kaden Elliss after fielding a top-10 defense last season.

The Saints won't be a juggernaut, but they will do enough to win the NFC South.

Prior to last season, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers had made the playoffs five straight seasons. But after a 6-2 start to the season, Tampa fell apart over the season's second half—just two wins the rest of the year.

There are multiple potential issues on offense, whether it's the skill positions, the O-Line or even the future of quarterback Baker Mayfield with the team. Tampa's defense ranked in the bottom half of the league last year in points allowed and doesn't look a bit better on paper in 2026.

If early losses start piling up, things could get ugly in Tampa by Halloween.

The Denver Broncos had the best record in the AFC last year. If quarterback Bo Nix didn't break his ankle in the playoffs, the Broncos may well have represented the conference in Super Bowl LX.

It starts with Denver's defense, which is among the league's best. The loss of edge-rusher Jonathon Cooper is a blow, but the Broncos are not going to be an easy team to score on.

Bo Nix appears to be 100 percent entering the league, and the Broncos gave him a shiny new toy in the passing game in wide receiver Jaylen Waddle.

There aren't many weaknesses in the Mile High City.

The Chiefs have been the AFC's most consistently dominant teams over the past decade—last year's 6-11 finish was the first time the team didn't win the AFC West since all the way back in 2015.

That dominance is reflected in this number. But it's also a tall ask.

Patrick Mahomes will start Week 1, but he's working back from an ACL tear and may not be 100 percent for a while. The entire Kansas City offense has been pedestrian as often as not the past two years, and with Travis Kelce all but certainly entering his final season the passing attack could again struggle to challenge defenses vertically.

The Chiefs are too good to post another sub-.500 season. But expecting a juggernaut is, again, a tall ask.

The city they play in may not have high expectations for the Raiders in 2026, but don't tell fans that—Fernando-Mania is sweeping through the fanbase after the Raiders drafted Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza first overall this year

It will be Kirk Cousins under center to start the season, and he'll lead an offense that includes running back Ashton Jeanty, tight end Brock Bowers and—that's it. The offensive line should be better, but that doesn't mean they will be good.

The defense still has edge-rusher Maxx Crosby, and the Raiders spent a ton on adding free agents on that side of the ball. That defense will be improved this season, but there's a lot of room for it.

The Los Angeles Chargers are one of the better teams in the league no mentioned a lot as one of the better teams in the league.

It's a team that could do real damage this season. Justin Herbert may not be an elite quarterback, but he isn't far off. The Chargers fielded one of the league's best defenses last year—the Chargers were a top-10 defense across the board and a top-five defense in terms of yards allowed.

But the same issue that plagued the Bolts last year threatens to do them again in 2026—the offensive line. A year ago, it was the tackles. This year, it's the interior of the offensive line that's the problem.

Not sure what's worse—the meager win total that was set for the Over/Under for the Cardinals this year or the fact that I'm pretty confident the under is going to hit.

There just isn't a lot to like about this team. The quarterback is a journeyman backup. Arizona has a pair of young skill-position players who were drafted in the top-five in recent years—one enters the season hurt, while the other has disappointed over his first two seasons.

The defense allowed the sixth-most yards and fourth-most points per game last year, and outside edge-rusher Josh Sweat and safety Budda Baker, it's a who's who of "Who?"

Arizona is absolutely in play for the first pick in 2027.

There is one path to Rams failing to win 12 games. Just one. Like Dr. Strange and Thanos.

The Rams just made the NFC Championship Game on the back of an offensive buzzsaw led by a quarterback who was named the NFL's Most Valuable Player. But the defense let them down at the end.

The Rams traded for a Pro Bowl cornerback in Trent McDuffie. Added the reigning Defensive Player of the Year in another trade for edge-rusher Myles Garrett. Then three-time DPOY Aaron Donald came out of retirement, because overkill.

If the Rams don't win Super Bowl LXI, the season will have been a failure. That's where the bar is now.

Generally speaking, it's folly to write off the San Francisco 49ers—despite being shredded by injuries in 2025, the Niners went 12-5 last year and won a playoff game.

Do it anyway—because at some point San Francisco's luck is going to run out.

The team is already dealing with multiple banged-up players expected to play big roles on both sides of the ball. That includes running back Christian McCaffrey, who is certain to regress after an NFL-high 413 touches a year ago.

San Francisco's two best defensive players (edge-rusher Nick Bosa and linebacker Fred warner) are both coming off major injuries. So is tight end George Kittle. The schedule in December is rough.

The 49ers won't be a bad team in 2026. But a backslide is coming.

The Seattle Seahawks don't look like the best team in the NFL on paper. They may not be the fifth-best team in the league on paper.

But the Seahawks are also the defending Super Bowl champions—because games are not played on paper.

Seattle isn't without its issues, whether it's a potential lack of depth in the secondary or questions at running back with Kenneth Walker gone and Zach Charbonnet on injured reserve to open the season.

But the Seahawks took steps to address those issues in the offseason, and last year at least Seattle was a team where the whole was greater than the sum of its parts.

The champs are good for 11 wins—at least.

articles.title: Titans' Jeffery Simmons to hit milestone against Jets in Week 1
articles.summary: Jeffery Simmons set to reach a milestone as the Tennessee Titans prepare for their season opener against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
It's hard to believe that the NFL regular season will be kicking off in less than a week, and at this point next week, the Tennessee Titans will be wrapping up game week preparations to take on the New York Jets .

There is no doubt that the season opener will be memorable for the Titans and their fans. Not only will Robert Saleh be making his Titans' debut against his former team to kick off the final season in Nissan Stadium, but Tennessee will also be inducting one of their legends, Chris Johnson, into the Titans' Ring of Honor. There will also be a minor milestone that has flown under the radar.

The NFL released the official game capsule for the Week 1 matchup against the Jets, and one of the notes annotated was that star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons was set to take part in his 100th game with the organization.

In a league where the average career for defensive tackles spans roughly five years, Simmons has not only surpassed that; he is playing the best football of his career heading into 2026 and is the unquestioned leader of the Titans' defense. And Simmons is showing no signs of slowing down.

Earlier this offseason, Simmons signed a then-record contract extension for defensive tackles, locking him up long-term in Nashville and setting him up to help the Titans dig out of the AFC South basement.
