articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft: 5 Edge rushers for the Eagles to watch
articles.summary: The Eagles have intriguing pieces at edge rusher, but the long-term picture remains fluid as they continue searching for pass-rushing talent.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles have invested heavily in their pass rush, but questions about the position's future aren't going away anytime soon. Jonathan Greenard was one of the biggest defensive additions this offseason . Yet, a pec injury suffered while lifting weights has prevented Eagles fans from seeing him practice or play in Vic Fangio's defense.

Jalyx Hunt looks like a rising star after a dominant training camp , while Nolan Smith enters a pivotal season as he tries to solidify his place in the team's long-term plans. Meanwhile, veteran additions Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa could become important contributors. Neither has established himself as a clear long-term answer.

With college football returning, here are five edge rushers who could begin working their way onto Philadelphia's radar as the 2027 NFL Draft cycle takes shape. Scouting has already begun. Here are some names to monitor.

Dylan Stewart might be the most naturally gifted pass rusher in the country. The South Carolina star followed an impressive freshman season with 33 tackles, 4.5 sacks, and three forced fumbles in 2025 while continuing to flash elite traits.

At 6-foot-5 and 245 pounds, he combines length, explosiveness, and athleticism that NFL teams covet. His sack numbers don't fully reflect the impact he has had on games. Another leap could cement him as one of the premier defensive prospects in the draft class.

Few edge rushers enter the season with more momentum than Colin Simmons. After recording nine sacks as a freshman, he exploded for 12 sacks, 43 tackles, and three forced fumbles in 2025 while earning All-America honors.

Simmons wins with speed, bend, and natural pass-rushing instincts that are difficult to teach. His ability to consistently affect quarterbacks makes him one of the favorites to be the first edge defender selected in 2027. Philadelphia will undoubtedly be watching.

Matayo Uiagalelei looks the part of an NFL edge rusher with a 6-foot-4, 266-pound frame and impressive athletic ability. He followed a 10.5-sack breakout campaign in 2024 with six sacks in 2025, though many evaluators expected even bigger production.

Consistency remains the biggest question surrounding his game. When he's locked in, Uiagalelei flashes first-round talent and the ability to dominate. If he puts everything together this season, his stock could rise quickly.

Clev Lubin has quietly produced everywhere he's played. After posting 9.5 sacks with Coastal Carolina Chanticleers in 2024, he transferred to Louisville and responded with 59 tackles and 8.5 sacks against stronger competition. The 267-pound defender plays with power, effort, and a knack for finding the football. His production over the past two seasons suggests he's more than just a one-year wonder. A strong 2026 campaign could push him into the national spotlight.

Wilson is one of the more fascinating names to monitor this season. The former Georgia Bulldogs recruit broke out with the Missouri Tigers with nine sacks in 2025 before transferring to Miami. At 6-foot-4 and 241 pounds, Wilson is a twitchy athlete who can threaten offensive tackles with speed off the edge. He remains somewhat raw but possesses the type of upside that NFL teams love to bet on. Another productive season could elevate him from intriguing prospect to legitimate first-round candidate.

Philadelphia's edge-rusher room has talent, but the long-term picture is still taking shape. Greenard has yet to play a snap for the Eagles, Hunt is emerging as a cornerstone piece, and important decisions could loom in the coming years regarding how the team allocates resources along the defensive front.

The Eagles have always prioritized premium positions, and few positions matter more than getting after the quarterback. That's why these five names are worth filing away as the road to the 2027 NFL Draft begins.

articles.title: 5 Best Fits for Mike Tomlin if Former Steelers HC Returns to NFL in 2027
articles.summary: After coaching for 25 years in the NFL, Mike Tomlin has transitioned into a broadcasting career, though he hasn't ruled out a return, fueling speculation about which team could lure him back to the sidelines.
articles.body:
After coaching for 25 years in the NFL, Mike Tomlin has transitioned into a broadcasting career, though he hasn't ruled out a return, fueling speculation about which team could lure him back to the sidelines.

During an interview on The Rich Eisen Show ( 2:00 mark ), Tomlin left the door open for a club to convince him back into the profession.

"I don't know about the long-term component of things," Tomlin said. "I've just lived enough to know to leave certain doors ajar."

So, let's first go through the logistics.

The Pittsburgh Steelers didn't fire Tomlin; he stepped down from his head-coaching position. So, the team still holds the rights to his contract, which runs through the 2027 season.

As a result, a club interested in Tomlin would have to trade for him, similar to how the Denver Broncos traded a 2023 first-rounder and a 2024 second-rounder to the New Orleans Saints for Sean Payton.

Tomlin's situation is slightly different than Payton's, though. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , the former Steelers head coach has a no-trade clause in his deal.

That said, there are five teams that could entice Tomlin to leave the broadcast booth and re-enter the head-coaching ranks next year.

From the outside looking in, the Carolina Panthers seem like a tough sell for Tomlin, who spent 19 years with the Steelers, because of the organizational turnover in recent years.

Also, the Panthers don't have a franchise quarterback. They exercised the fifth-year option in Bryce Young's rookie deal, but according to The Athletic's Joseph Person , the team isn't expected to sign him to an extension before the start of the season.

If Young and the Panthers struggle, the club may want a reset in leadership positions, including the general manager and/or head coach.

Yes, Carolina made the playoffs in the previous campaign, but the team lost three of its last four games and finished the season at 8-9.

Head coach Dave Canales isn't on the hot seat after winning a division title, but if Carolina regresses, owner David Tepper may at least look for an upgrade. Postseason appearance or not, a lead skipper with three consecutive losing seasons should be up for evaluation at his position.

Tomlin has expertise on the defensive side of the ball and may be intrigued by the addition of Pro Bowl linebacker Devin Lloyd, edge-rusher Jaelan Phillips and rookie second-round defensive tackle Lee Hunter. The Panthers could also give him some say-so on how to handle the quarterback position.

Lastly, Carolina plays in arguably the league's weakest division, which gives Tomlin a shot at a quick turnaround with immediate results.

Indianapolis Colts brass should be on the hot seat, particularly Chris Ballard. On his watch, the team hasn't made the playoffs since 2021 and has four winning seasons in nine years. In back-to-back campaigns, Indianapolis fell slightly below the .500 mark at 8-9.

If the Colts fire Ballard, the new general manager may want to handpick his head coach, raising questions about Shane Steichen's job security entering the fourth year of his deal, which runs through the 2028 season .

Tomlin may be hesitant to take the Colts job because the club traded its first-round pick to the New York Jets in a blockbuster deal for Sauce Gardner. Without that pick, Indianapolis could also lose out on a bidding competition for him.

On a positive note, the Colts have roster building blocks on offense. They signed running back Jonathan Taylor to a two-year extension. Wideout Alec Pierce signed a new four-year deal.

According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the team's contract talks with three-time first-team All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson are stagnant, though that could change in the coming weeks.

Quarterback Daniel Jones just signed a two-year extension, but Indianapolis can cut him and save $38 million in cap space next offseason, per Over the Cap .

If Tomlin has a long-term vision for the Colts' quarterback situation, he could coach up the defense and field a strong contender in 2027. Indianapolis could offer him personnel power to sweeten its offer.

While it would be an early dismissal for second-year head coach Aaron Glenn, another abysmal season could raise the temperature on his seat.

Last season, the New York Jets finished 3-14. If Gang Green doesn't at least make steps in the right direction with widespread turnover on the defensive side of the ball, which is Glenn's expertise, the team could look for another defensive-minded lead skipper with a big personality.

After hiring first-time lead skippers Robert Saleh and Glenn, the Jets can target someone who has a proven resume. Tomlin, a Super Bowl-winning head coach who led the Steelers to wins in 63 percent of games over 19 years, fits the bill.

Gang Green can offer one of its three first-round picks to the Steelers for Tomlin and still rebuild its roster with the addition of a quarterback and another blue-chip prospect on Day 1 of the 2027 draft.

Tomlin is already familiar with safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, who played six seasons in Pittsburgh, and he would have a seasoned field general in linebacker Demario Davis on defense. Rookie edge-rusher David Bailey has the potential to be a star.

In the event that New York moves on from Glenn, it would have the draft and roster assets to attract a big-name hire like Tomlin if he's ready for a return to the coaching ranks.

Bold Trade Predictions Before Season Kickoff 🏈

1 Reason Why Commanders' Fans Should Be Optimistic 🙏

Tampa Bay Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles should be on the hot seat entering the 2026 season.

Sure, the Buccaneers won three consecutive NFC South titles before they failed to make the playoffs last season, but the club has only one playoff win to show for it. Also, Tampa Bay is a mediocre 35-33 on Bowles' watch in a bottom-tier division.

Lastly, the Buccaneers' defense has regressed over the last two years, ranking 16th or worse in both scoring and total yards allowed. Keep in mind that Bowles is a defensive-minded head coach.

If Tampa Bay misses out on the postseason in consecutive years, Bowles may be on the way out, and Tomlin could be on the way back to where his pro coaching career started in 2001 on former Buccaneers head coach Tony Dungy's staff.

Tomlin could make a full-circle career move going back to Tampa Bay, though it also makes sense in a winnable division if he's able to retain quarterback Baker Mayfield, who's entering the final year of his contract.

Despite the loss of wideout Mike Evans in free agency and linebacker Lavonte David's retirement, the Buccaneers have enough talent to reclaim their spot atop the division, which is why Bowles should be under pressure this year.

If Bowles doesn't help this team rebound from a losing season, general manager Jason Licht may believe Tomlin can do a better job.

In head coach Dan Quinn's first year with the Washington Commanders, he led the team to the NFC Championship Game with then-rookie quarterback Jayden Daniels, but the club fell from 12-5 that year to 5-12 last season.

In addition to a significant fall in the standings, Quinn dismissed offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury and hired first-year play-caller David Blough to replace him.

Because of the Commanders' deep playoff run in the 2024 campaign, Quinn likely bought himself extra time, but it's concerning that he parted ways with his offensive coordinator after one year. In doing so, he raises questions about the construction of his coaching staff.

Quinn's job security is also tied to Daniels' development.

In 2025, Daniels missed 10 games due to injuries, which stunted his second-year growth, and only completed 60.6 percent of his passes. Still, after he won 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year, he goes into his third campaign garnering high expectations. If Quinn's offensive assistants aren't able to get the best out of him, the front office could consider more coaching changes.

After Ben Roethlisberger retired in 2022, Pittsburgh struggled offensively under Tomlin, but with a young franchise quarterback already in place, he may see better results on that side of the ball with the Commanders.

Maurice Moton covers the NFL for Bleacher Report. You can follow him on Twitter @MoeMoton .

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes’ father makes emotional court request as Chiefs star closes in on comeback after devastating injury
articles.summary: NFL News: Pat Mahomes Sr. is hoping to be in the stands when his son takes the field for the Kansas City Chiefs this season. The former MLB pitcher has asked a .
articles.body: Pat Mahomes Sr. is hoping to be in the stands when his son takes the field for the Kansas City Chiefs this season. The former MLB pitcher has asked a Texas court for permission to travel to several states during his ongoing probation. His request comes as Patrick Mahomes prepares for a crucial return after a serious knee injury ended his 2025 campaign earlier than expected.Pat Mahomes Sr. seeks court approval to attend Chiefs gamesAccording to a report by KTRE 9’s Nic Huber, Mahomes Sr. filed a motion in the 7th District Court in Tyler seeking approval to travel for seven NFL games during the 2026 season. His proposed destinations include Kansas City, Missouri, Las Vegas, Nevada, and Cincinnati, Ohio.The request is tied to his five-year probation sentence, which began after a 2024 DWI conviction. Because he remains under supervision, traveling outside Texas requires court approval and comes with specific conditions.Mahomes Sr. has already received permission for out-of-state travel this year. In June, he was allowed to visit Missouri to support his granddaughter Sterling, Patrick Mahomes’ five-year-old daughter, during her first dance recital.The conditions attached to that trip included reporting to his probation officer before leaving and completing a urinalysis test. Similar requirements could apply to his latest request. The filing states that Mahomes Sr. understands he may have to undergo testing before and after his trips whenever his supervision officer requests it.His court filing also points to steps he has taken during probation. He has completed 160 hours of community service and attended a 16-week outpatient treatment program at Cenikor.The legal scrutiny surrounding Mahomes Sr. dates back several years. He pleaded guilty to a DWI charge in 2018 and served 40 days in county jail. His 2024 arrest came shortly before Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs secured another Super Bowl victory.A later incident also complicated his probation. His ankle monitor reportedly recorded a TAC level of 0.045% on January 1, leading to another arrest. However, a hair follicle test reportedly came back clean, and the court declined to revoke his probation. His supervision period was subsequently extended from five years to seven.Patrick Mahomes' Week 1 return adds urgency to requestMahomes Sr.’s request comes at an important moment for Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs quarterback is working his way back from the ACL and LCL injuries he suffered against the Los Angeles Chargers on December 14, 2025.His rehabilitation has involved more than simply getting back on the field. Kansas City has managed his workload carefully throughout the offseason, while head coach Andy Reid kept him out of preseason action.One particularly personal detail from Mahomes’ recovery emerged recently. According to Kansas City Star reporter Sam McDowell, Mahomes had a simple goal after returning to Kansas City:“After he returned to Kansas City later in the week, he shared with some of those closest to him a more immediate goal for his recovery,” The Kansas City Star’s Sam McDowell wrote in a Mahomes recovery feature on September 4. “He wanted to walk before his baby daughter, 11-month-old Golden.”Now, the focus is shifting toward Week 1. NFL Network's Tom Pelissero indicated that Mahomes has a chance to play against the Denver Broncos, although Reid has yet to officially confirm his status.“At this point Andy Reid has not even confirmed that Patrick Mahomes is starting in week one,” Pellisero said to Rich Eisen. “I would say all signs are pointing toward Patrick Mahomes being out there.”If the court grants Mahomes Sr.’s request, he could have the opportunity to watch his son begin another NFL season in person. For a father who has closely followed Patrick’s career, those seven games would mean far more than simply traveling to watch football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce expands business empire with $53 Million hydration drink partnership while chasing another Super Bowl with Chiefs
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce was already looking beyond football when the 2025 NFL season approached. Last September, just days before the Kansas City Chiefs opened t.
articles.body: Travis Kelce was already looking beyond football when the 2025 NFL season approached. Last September, just days before the Kansas City Chiefs opened their campaign in Brazil, the star tight end added another business venture to his growing portfolio. Kelce announced a partnership with organic hydration company Recover 180, taking on roles as both an investor and brand partner while preparing for another demanding NFL season.Travis Kelce added Recover 180 to his business portfolio in 2025The announcement came on September 2, 2025, as Kelce prepared for his 13th NFL season. His timing was notable. The Chiefs were set to face the Los Angeles Chargers in São Paulo, and Kelce was focused on returning to form after a 2024 season he viewed as below his usual standard.Rather than simply attaching his name to another product, Kelce joined Recover 180 as an investor. The move fit a pattern that had become increasingly clear in his career. His influence stretched well beyond the football field, with business interests and partnerships spanning fashion, fitness, food and lifestyle brands.Kelce had also recently launched a collection with American Eagle alongside athletes such as Jeremiah Smith, Drew Allar, Suni Lee and Kiyan Anthony. His wider portfolio included partnerships with Patrón, Hydrow and General Mills. He also co-owned Garage Beer with his brother, Jason Kelce.Speaking about the Recover 180 partnership last year, Kelce said:“When it comes to performing at your highest level, quality matters,” Kelce said. “I’ve been drinking RECOVER 180 because it’s clean, organic hydration with ingredients that support peak performance. Having a healthier recovery option is a game-changer, and I love investing in something that’s truly pushing the category forward.”The brand also highlighted why Kelce was a natural fit for its plans. Boardroom described the three-time Super Bowl champion as someone whose athletic career and public profile could help introduce the company to a broader audience.Travis Kelce reveals Patrick Mahomes influenced his decision to return to Chiefs this year Travis Kelce has revealed that Patrick Mahomes’ determination during his recovery played a major role in his decision to continue playing for the Kansas City Chiefs this year. Mahomes suffered a serious injury, underwent surgery and worked relentlessly to return to the field, determined to help Kansas City compete for another Super Bowl.While the Chiefs may not enter the season as overwhelming favorites, Kelce believes Mahomes’ mindset gives the team a strong chance of contending. Speaking about his quarterback, Kelce said he could see Mahomes’ determination and frustration over how the previous season unfolded.That mindset reportedly influenced Kelce’s decision not to retire. Kelce explained that knowing Mahomes and seeing what he was going through became a “huge reason” why he remains in the NFL, adding that he wants to be there for his longtime teammate “in every aspect of the game.”Mahomes and Kelce have developed one of the NFL’s most successful partnerships, both on and off the field. Kelce’s comments highlight the personal bond between the two stars and show how much Mahomes’ comeback means to him. As the new season approaches, their continued partnership could once again become central to Kansas City’s championship hopes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the three time Super Bowl Most Valuable Player, has spent the last nine months in recovery as he has tried his best to heal his body and mind after the severe injuries he sustained in Week 15 of the last season at the Week 15’s loss against the Los Angeles Rams. With the new season beginning in the next few weeks, it seems Patrick Mahomes had a goal in mind related to his children that helped him recover.Patrick Mahomes had only one goal in his mind related to his daughter as he spent time in recovery ahead of the new seasonA few hours ago, Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star, reported that Patrick Mahomes wanted to walk before his newborn, Golden Raye, could take her first steps.Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star noted, "After he returned to Kansas City later in the week, he shared with some of those closest to him a more immediate goal for his recovery. He wanted to walk before his baby daughter, 11-month-old Golden.”Sam McDowell of the Kansas City Star added, “Her first birthday was approaching. It's exciting. I didn't know if I was going to have to take days off, but my body has responded the right way. articles.title: Is Arch Manning thinking about the 2027 NFL Draft? Peyton and Eli Manning gave him one important message
articles.summary: NFL News: Arch Manning cannot really escape NFL questions. His last name guarantees that much, and the 2027 NFL Draft conversation has already started before hi.
articles.body: Arch Manning cannot really escape NFL questions. His last name guarantees that much, and the 2027 NFL Draft conversation has already started before his second full season as the Texas Longhorns’ starting quarterback.His uncles, Peyton Manning and Eli Manning, have given him a much simpler assignment. Enjoy college. PEOPLE's Skyler Caruso published an exclusive interview with Arch on Sept. 5, though the conversation took place during the Miami Grand Prix in early May.What did Peyton and Eli Manning tell Arch Manning about the 2027 NFL Draft?Arch said both of his uncles have spoken to him about this stage of his career.Their message did not involve draft boards, NFL teams or where he could eventually be selected.“Yeah, a lot of advice,” Arch told PEOPLE. “They ultimately just told me to enjoy college right now, worry about that when the time comes, just take it day by day and try to be a good guy.”That advice comes from two quarterbacks who know exactly what waits on the other side.Peyton became the No. 1 overall pick in the 1998 NFL Draft and later entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Eli also went No. 1 overall, in 2004, before spending his NFL career with the New York Giants.Arch has given no public commitment about entering the 2027 NFL Draft.When PEOPLE spoke with him shortly after the 2026 NFL Draft, he stayed noncommittal about whether he would declare next year. His focus remained on Texas.“Trying to make the most out of it,” Manning said of the upcoming season. “Do whatever I can to help the team win and have a good time.”That approach follows a 2025 season in which Manning became Texas’ full-time starter. The Longhorns finished 10-3.He also admitted that his first year in charge gave him plenty to process.“Got an in-game experience, there were ups and downs, but ultimately learned from it and excited for this year,” Manning said.One of those difficult moments came immediately.Texas opened the 2025 season with a 14-7 road loss to the Ohio State Buckeyes. Eli later told PEOPLE he was proud of how his nephew handled the environment and stayed in the game.The attention around Arch has only increased since then.Why is the NFL conversation already following Arch Manning into the 2026 season?Manning enters 2026 with two stories developing at the same time. Texas needs him now. The NFL might want him next.PEOPLE described Manning as an expected top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, while other early projections have already begun connecting him with quarterback-needy teams. One Sept. 5 report from Marca discussed the Arizona Cardinals as a possible destination while stressing that the draft remains far away.That distinction matters.Arizona's eventual draft position is unknown. Manning has not declared. An entire college football season still sits between the current speculation and any 2027 NFL decision.For Manning, the immediate calendar is much simpler.Texas opens its 2026 season against the Texas State Bobcats on Sept. 5. It will be Manning's second year as the Longhorns' full-time starter and another chance to build on what he learned in 2025.His offseason comments also suggest he understands how quickly the NFL discussion can swallow everything around a highly rated college quarterback.When he spoke with PEOPLE in May, Manning said he planned to use his time away from football to return to New Orleans, spend time with friends and decompress.“I love to play golf, hang out with my buddies and just be a regular dude,” Manning said.The NFL questions are not disappearing. Neither is the Manning name attached to them.For now, Peyton and Eli have told their nephew exactly where to keep his attention: Texas, one day at a time.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How Travis Kelce turned a childhood love for Roller Coasters into a 9% stake in Six Flags
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce grew up as a Cleveland Heights kid who knew Cedar Point the way most Ohio kids do: summer trips, sunburns, and arguments about which coas.
articles.body: Travis Kelce grew up as a Cleveland Heights kid who knew Cedar Point the way most Ohio kids do: summer trips, sunburns, and arguments about which coaster was better. He favored Raptor. His brother Jason swore by Millennium Force. Neither of them could have imagined, back then, that those family trips to Sandusky would one day lead Kelce to co-own a piece of North America's largest regional amusement park operator. Yet here we are. In October 2025, Kelce joined activist investor firm JANA Partners and two other high-profile business figures to acquire roughly 9% of Six Flags Entertainment Corporation.Why did Travis Kelce invest in Six Flags?The investment wasn't random. Kelce had been openly nostalgic about Cedar Point for years on the New Heights podcast, often sparring with Jason about their favorite rides. When JANA Partners came knocking, the opportunity wasn't just financial. It was personal. Kelce said it himself: "So crazy to even imagine this is real, but you gotta love it when life comes full circle."But make no mistake, this wasn't a celebrity vanity deal. JANA Partners has a serious track record. They were the firm behind the push that eventually forced Whole Foods to sell to Amazon. Joining Kelce in the investment group were Glenn Murphy, a former CEO of GAP, and Dave Habiger, a technology executive with Reddit ties. These are not soft hands at the table.The timing mattered too. Six Flags stock had crashed nearly 70% from above $55 per share following its 2024 merger with Cedar Fair, falling to around $14. Attendance dropped 5.6% in the first half of 2026 alone. Revenue fell. Two parks closed for good after the 2025 season. The company was, by most measures, struggling to stay afloat under a $5 billion debt load. When the JANA announcement landed, Six Flags shares surged more than 17% in a single day. Markets read the news as a signal that change was coming, whether management liked it or not.By March 2026, Kelce's relationship with Six Flags deepened further. The company named him brand ambassador, placing him across social media, broadcast campaigns, streaming platforms, and in-park promotions throughout the year. He later partnered with Cedar Point and Kings Island to promote 2027 season pass sales. "Growing up, our family spent a lot of time at Cedar Point and Kings Island, and these parks have given us some unforgettable memories," Kelce said. "I want other families to experience all the same fun we did."Is Travis Kelce's Six Flags investment a smart financial move?That's the harder question. Sentimental backstory aside, Six Flags is still a company with serious structural problems. Attendance keeps sliding. The Cedar Fair merger, expected to boost foot traffic by 6%, delivered the opposite result. Regional theme parks are especially vulnerable when household budgets tighten, and unlike Disney, Six Flags doesn't have the pricing power, global diversification, or intellectual property to cushion the blows.What JANA is betting on is that operational changes, better guest experience investment, and pressure on leadership can shift that trajectory. Kelce brings something specific to that equation: reach. His crossover appeal, from NFL fans to Taylor Swift's fanbase to Middle America families, is genuine and quantifiable. Six Flags CEO John Reilly put it plainly: "His fun-loving personality, commitment to excellence and passion for the game have contributed to three Super Bowl titles on the field, and we're confident they will score big with our guests as well."Whether Kelce's star power can move turnstile numbers remains to be seen. But the investment itself is a telling window into how he's building wealth outside football. Baseball team ownership with the Cleveland Guardians. Formula 1 investments. The $100 million podcast deal. Hot sauce. Beer. And now, roller coasters. The kid from Cleveland Heights isn't just collecting trophies anymore.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football Mock Draft Ideal Scenarios, Selections for 12-Team League
articles.summary: Every fantasy football draft offers an opportunity to pave a path toward championship glory.
articles.body:
Every fantasy football draft offers an opportunity to pave a path toward championship glory.

While most won't lead anywhere close to that, there are a number of different ways to hit pay dirt.

Just like NFL contenders comprise all different pay styles, fantasy juggernauts can feature a vast array of builds. And yet, we still feel like there's a right way to approach things—at each and every pick on the board, in fact.

To help show what we mean, we'll walk through a three-round guide for every pick spot in a 12-team league.

This is easy: Grab your favorite of Bijan Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs—Robinson for us, Gibbs for many—and then plan on collecting pass-catchers at the 2/3 turn. Given the lack of depth at running back, the position may not look change much between the third and fourth rounds.

While we aren't actually copying and pasting the Pick 1 strategy, the guide is almost identical. Take whoever of Robinson or Gibbs doesn't go No. 1, and then rule out running backs for the next two rounds unless an obvious target falls.

Here's where a mini-run on receivers will start, and it should start with Ja'Marr Chase. With a healthy Joe Burrow back running the show, Chase should be in line for a monster season. A Round 2 running back would make sense if the draft board allows (i.e., still features someone like Derrick Henry, Chase Brown or Kenneth Walker III), but otherwise plan on grabbing two more pass-catchers.

Puka Nacua is up next on the priority list, although Jaxon Smith-Njigba has a case to be made, too. Your odds of having a viable running back in Round 2 should let it happen, but don't force the issue by reaching on Kyren Williams or Jeremiyah Love. Ashton Jeanty could be a great get if you're comfortable with his injury reports . In Round 3, then, you'd want the best wide receiver or tight end on the board.

If Smith-Njigba is still on the board, then he's an obvious target here. Ideally, you're getting a running back in Round 2 (maybe Henry, Walker or Jeanty) and targeting a pass-catcher in Round 3.

This might be the sweet spot for Christian McCaffrey. There is obvious risk with a 30-year-old running back coming off of a 450-touch season, but the ceiling is too rich to let him fall any farther. Protect yourself with a second-round running back, and then grab the top receiver available in Round 3.

The target here is Amon-Ra St. Brown, who cracks the short list of fantasy football's safest players. Because he's such a sure thing, you could try double-tapping running back in Rounds 2 and 3. Chase Brown or De'Von Achane could start it, and then Jeanty or even Javonte Williams could finish it.

The targets get less obvious the farther you move down the draft board, but Jonathan Taylor gets our nod. Running back arguably takes a little tier drop behind him, so you'd be smart to add him before that happens. And since you'd have such a strong option at running back, you'd be flexible enough to go best player available with your next few picks.

This is a coin flip call between CeeDee Lamb and Justin Jefferson, so just go with your favorite here. Unless Taylor, Saquon Barkley or James Cook III makes it back to you in Round 2, you might want to triple up on pass-catchers before targeting a running back in Round 4.

You can get the other side of the coin here with either of Lamb or Jefferson. Running back should be a compelling option in Round 2 (Barkley, Cook, Brown, Achane or Omarion Hampton), and then the foundation can support best player available in Round 3.

This should be the right spot for a risk-reward wager in James Cook III. He seems like a touchdown regression candidate after tallying 32 scores the past two seasons, but you could live with a few less end-zone trips at this price. Going WR/WR is probably the right way to handle Rounds 2 and 3, but Jeanty would be tempting if he's available in the third.

Closing out the first round with Saquon Barkley could prove a stroke of brilliance. Regression felt entirely possible in 2025, and that unfortunately defined his season. For those who may not remember, though, his 2024 output featured 2,283 scrimmage yards and 15 scores. After Barkley, you could double-tap running back with Brown or Achane if you're bullish on either, or you could go WR/WR in Rounds 2 and 3 if you're not.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes’ life with Brittany looks completely different once the cameras stop following the Chiefs quarterback
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes is returning from a torn ACL and LCL, signed a new record-breaking contract, attended Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's wedding, watched.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes is returning from a torn ACL and LCL, signed a new record-breaking contract, attended Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift's wedding, watched the FIFA World Cup Final from MetLife Stadium, and still made it to a Kansas City back-to-school food allergy event with Bronze in tow. That offseason alone tells you something. The version of Mahomes the public sees on Sundays is only part of the picture. The fuller one is built around three kids, a genuine partnership with Brittany, and a family life that runs on its own terms.What does Patrick Mahomes actually do when he is not playing football?The easy assumption is that an NFL quarterback's offseason is mostly about workouts and sponsorship shoots. For Mahomes, that is barely half of it.When CommunityAmerica Credit Union recently filmed a new commercial with the family, one scene had the 6-foot-2 quarterback sitting inside a children's playhouse, pretending to sip tea. That is not a planned PR stunt. That is just Tuesday for a father of three who has clearly stopped trying to maintain any image of being untouchable.During training camp, Brittany brought Sterling, Bronze, and Golden to the preseason game against the Rams, all three dressed in Chiefs red. "Their faces when they see their dad," she posted, "and bronze yawning is just the best." The comment sounds offhand, but it captures something real. The kids do not understand what it means to be Patrick Mahomes. They just know he is dad, and he is back.That backdrop matters more than it gets credit for. Mahomes spent the months after his December knee surgery not just rehabbing but rebuilding some version of normal. The family visited Legoland in Carlsbad and SeaWorld in San Diego. They spent a weekend at a Texas farm with friends and family, feeding baby goats, roasting s'mores, and paddleboarding. Brittany called it "the best weekend with our squad." There were no Chiefs jerseys in those photos. Just five people on a trip.When Brittany took the kids to a tropical resort in August while Patrick remained at camp, he was following along on Instagram and left a comment on her post. That one detail is quietly telling. He could not be there. He noticed anyway.How are Patrick and Brittany Mahomes raising their kids away from the spotlight?The most consistent and least discussed part of the Mahomes household is how deliberately they have built a life around their children's actual needs rather than their public image.Both Sterling and Bronze have food allergies. Bronze had a severe reaction to peanut powder as an infant that sent the family to the emergency room. Brittany had Sterling's AUVI-q epinephrine injector on hand at the time. "Knowing that I did have that with me, I felt a little more competent in the situation," she recalled. That experience did not become a brand moment right away. It became a cause. The couple has partnered with FARE, Food Allergy Research and Education, multiple times through their 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. This summer, Patrick and Brittany attended the back-to-school event with Bronze, not just for photos but actually mingling with families throughout the day.According to FARE, roughly one in 13 children in the United States lives with a food allergy. That statistic gives the Mahomes' involvement real scale. They are not the only family managing this. They just happen to be one of the most visible.Brittany, for her part, has built a separate professional life that runs parallel to Patrick's. KC Current Studios officially opened its doors on August 3, marking a significant milestone for the NWSL club that the couple co-owns. She landed the 2026 SI Swimsuit digital cover. She came back from a fractured back stronger than before. None of that happened because Patrick Mahomes is her husband. It happened because she put in the work.The cameras follow the Chiefs quarterback. But the life he is actually living is much quieter, and by design.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: What ‘chaos’ is Kelly Stafford bracing for before Matthew Stafford’s Rams opener vs. 49ers?
articles.summary: NFL News: Kelly Stafford knows the quiet part of September is nearly over.Days before Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams begin their 2026 NFL season in A.
articles.body: Kelly Stafford knows the quiet part of September is nearly over.Days before Matthew Stafford and the Los Angeles Rams begin their 2026 NFL season in Australia, Kelly shared photos from a Lake Tahoe getaway with her husband. Her caption was only two sentences, but the timing said plenty about what comes next.Why did Kelly Stafford call her trip with Matthew Stafford ‘a reset before the chaos’?Kelly posted several photos from the couple’s trip to Homewood in Lake Tahoe on Friday. The pictures included the Staffords sitting together by the lake, selfies, lakeside moments, and time aboard a private yacht.She summed up the trip simply on Instagram. “A reset before the chaos. I just love this man.”The “chaos” is arriving quickly.Matthew and the Rams are scheduled to open their regular season against the San Francisco 49ers on Sept. 10 at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in Melbourne, Australia.The matchup sends Los Angeles across the Pacific for Week 1 before the rest of a schedule Kelly has already described as difficult for their family.The couple has four daughters, and Kelly previously addressed what the Rams’ 2026 schedule could mean at home. In an Aug. 17 Instagram Story, she reacted after taking stock of Los Angeles’ travel, holiday games and prime-time appearances.“My just now realizing the Rams play in Australia, play on Christmas, play on Thanksgiving Eve, have 7 (possibly more) prime time games, and DON'T HAVE A REAL BYE WEEK. Parenting this season will be such a joy,” Kelly wrote.That makes the Lake Tahoe caption less cryptic than it first appears. The Staffords were taking time together immediately before a season that begins thousands of miles from Los Angeles and comes with an unusually demanding calendar for their family.For Matthew, it will also mark the start of his 18th NFL season.Why does family time matter so much to Matthew Stafford during an NFL season?Matthew has spoken directly about the role Kelly and their daughters play in allowing him to continue his career.During an August appearance with Greg Olsen on “Youth Inc.,” Stafford called his family “the most important thing in my life.” He also credited Kelly with handling much of what happens at home while his NFL schedule takes him away.“They are incredible supporters of mine, backbone to what I do, also the thing that gives me the most perspective in life. I love playing this game,” Stafford said.He explained that the attention he receives as an NFL quarterback does not carry the same weight as the people waiting for him at home.“People chant your your name or they cheer for you and all that out there in a stadium. But the people that matter to me the most are the people, when I get home, and they give me the most honest feedback and the most loving feedback.”Stafford also said he tries to build his daughters into his football routine whenever possible. He brings them to breakfast at the team facility on Tuesdays before taking them to school and makes a point of being home for dinner when he is in town.That balance has also become part of Stafford's relationship with Rams head coach Sean McVay.Stafford said McVay understands the importance of giving him opportunities to spend time with his family. The quarterback went further, saying that flexibility has helped extend his career.“And I, frankly, wouldn’t still be playing this game if that wasn’t the case. And so I appreciate him for that and my family for that.”Now the regular season is here.The Rams reached the NFC Championship Game last season, and Stafford is preparing for another run with Los Angeles. Before the meetings, flights, games and travel begin, Kelly’s photos captured something much smaller: a few days with her husband while his calendar still allowed it.“A reset before the chaos” was not just a cute vacation caption. For the Stafford family, the schedule explains exactly what she meant.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 2027 NFL Draft: 7 wide receivers who could fit the Ravens
articles.summary: The headliner of this class may not be a Ravens option, but several emerging NCAA playmakers could attract Baltimore's attention.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens aren't entering the 2026 season desperate for wide receiver help, but that doesn't mean the position can be ignored. Zay Flowers has developed into one of the NFL's most dangerous playmakers, though injuries have occasionally interrupted some of his momentum this offseason . The Ravens are also encouraged by what they've seen from Ja'Kobi Lane .

The latter has burst onto the scene and quickly generated excitement . Whether that early success proves sustainable over a full season remains to be seen.

Beyond those two, there are still questions. Rashod Bateman needs a strong season after an inconsistent stretch of play, while Devontez Walker, LaJohntay Wester, and Elijah Sarratt would all be welcome breakout options. Baltimore hopes one or more of those young receivers emerges , but Eric DeCosta has never stopped scouting future solutions simply because a position appears stable.

Jeremiah Smith is the obvious headliner in the 2027 NCAA draft class. Unless something unexpected happens, he'll likely be long gone before Baltimore makes its first selection. Still, he's worth mentioning alongside several other receivers who could begin attracting attention throughout the upcoming college football season.

Cam Coleman enters the season with enormous expectations after transferring from Auburn.

The 6-foot-3 receiver flashed star potential during his time with the Tigers, showcasing the size and athleticism NFL teams covet on the outside. He totaled 56 receptions for 708 yards and five touchdowns in 2025 after an impressive freshman campaign. If Texas unlocks another level of production, Coleman could cement himself as one of the premier receivers in the draft class.

Charlie Becker may not receive the same national attention as some of the bigger names, but NFL scouts are already paying close attention.

The 6-foot-3 playmaker averaged more than 20 yards per reception last season, turning 34 catches into 679 yards and four touchdowns. His ability to stretch defenses vertically stands out immediately, and his combination of size and speed gives him one of the higher ceilings among receivers in this class.

Ravens fans don't need much imagination to picture how Ryan Williams would fit alongside Lamar Jackson. Williams wins with explosiveness, acceleration, and the ability to turn routine touches into big plays. He posted 689 receiving yards and four touchdowns in 2025 after a breakout freshman season. Like Flowers, the biggest remaining questions are about his frame, but few receivers in the country possess his game-breaking ability.

Nick Marsh has quietly become one of the more intriguing receiver prospects in college football. After transferring to Indiana, the former Michigan State Spartans standout enters the season with significant momentum. He recorded 59 receptions for 662 yards and six touchdowns in 2025 and continues to flash the size and upside NFL teams love on the perimeter. Another leap could push him firmly into first-round discussions.

Bryant Wesco may be one of the biggest wild cards in the class.

The Clemson receiver has produced steadily through his first two seasons while flashing the traits of a future NFL starter. After earning Freshman All-American honors, he followed with another productive campaign in 2025. If his development continues, Wesco could emerge as one of the fastest-rising receivers in college football.

Few prospects are built like Nyck Harbor. At 6-foot-5 and 235 pounds, Harbor looks more like a tight end until he starts running. His rare combination of size and speed has fascinated scouts for years. Production has not always matched the physical gifts, but if Harbor finally puts everything together this season, his draft stock could skyrocket.

If there is a seventh name worth monitoring, it's Texas receiver Ryan Wingo. The Second-Team All-SEC selection possesses the size, speed, and upside to join the top tier of this receiver class. Playing alongside Coleman could limit some opportunities. Time will tell, but NFL scouts will have plenty of reasons to keep Wingo on their radar throughout the season.

It's early, but Baltimore could be watching

The Ravens may discover they already have enough answers at wide receiver. Lane could continue ascending. Bateman could deliver his best season yet. Walker, Wester, and Sarratt could carve out larger roles.

Still, Baltimore has consistently invested in pass catchers around Lamar Jackson, and Eric DeCosta has never been afraid to plan a year ahead. If the Ravens decide another playmaker is needed in 2027, several names on this list could find themselves firmly on Baltimore's radar by season's end, and these are some outstanding men to keep an eye on.

articles.title: From Tunsil’s injury to passive approach at center, fans are losing sleep over Commanders’ OL - Poll Results
articles.summary: Fans are concerned As the Washington Commanders prepare to kick off the 2026 NFL campaign, the collective mood of the fan base is suspended somewhere between...
articles.body:
As the Washington Commanders prepare to kick off the 2026 NFL campaign, the collective mood of the fan base is suspended somewhere between fragile optimism and overwhelming anxiety. In this week's Reacts poll conducted by Hogs Haven, readers were asked to pinpoint their primary concern regarding the team heading into the new season.

The results were overwhelmingly focused on one area: 65% of respondents stated that offensive line skill and depth is the biggest worry, while 11% identified the job done by general manager Adam Peters as their chief concern. By contrast, 9% of the fan base reported pure excitement for the new season, unburdened by dread of roster or other shortcomings.

The interconnected anxiety about the roster & the front office

On the surface, the low percentage of fans explicitly pointing their fingers at general manager Adam Peters might suggest a high level of trust for AP. However, constructing a football roster is a tightly woven ecosystem. It seems likely that the 11% who identify the GM as the primary concern are judging him largely through the lens of having failed to build an effective roster, with the offensive line featuring prominently in that negative assessment. In other words, the anxiety surrounding the front office and the anxiety surrounding the five men up front are largely the same conversation. The perceived failure of roster execution in his three years at the helm — and specifically this offseason — is where negative critiques of Peters tend to focus.

A tale of two worries: The center and left tackle woes

The fan base's high anxiety revolves primarily around two glaring issues along the line – issues of very different origins. One was due to injury, which is part and parcel of the NFL, while the other appears to have been at least partly self-inflicted.

The most scrutinized sequence of events this offseason started when the front office made the bold choice to cut Tyler Biadasz several days before the start of free agency. While moving on from a starter is not uncommon in the NFL, the subsequent plan (or failure of the plan) raised eyebrows.

Peters failed to secure a definitive, high-tier upgrade at center through free agency or the early rounds of the draft. Instead, the front office handed the keys to veteran guard Nick Allegretti, banking on him to be a healthy, consistent starter – even now, despite a lingering calf injury that cost him nearly all of training camp.

Exacerbating this gamble was the failure to secure a proven backup. Should Allegretti's injury flare back up, the primary reinforcement is rookie sixth-round draft pick Matt Gulbin . Relying on a late-round rookie and an injured converted guard to solidify the interior protection appears to be a flashing red light for roughly two-thirds or three-quarters of our survey respondents.

The secondary crisis arose when star left tackle Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps midway through training camp, an unavoidable and unfortunate injury that weakens both starter and backup at two positions — left tackle and left guard — entering the season.

The critical differences between the two issues are that the tackle position was backed up with talented depth, and the trigger was an unavoidable injury. Looked at in one light, it actually indicates good roster planning. Things are very different with the depth chart for the center position, the avoidability of the precipitating event, and the roster approach of the front office.

What makes the center situation so frustrating for the Hogs Haven community is that Adam Peters demonstrated proactivity at other positions. When roster holes or depth issues became apparent late in the summer, the front office took action:

Brought in elite veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs to bolster the receiver group.

Secured veteran cornerbacks Rasul Douglas and Fabian Moreau to steady the secondary.

Signed veteran tackle D.J. Humphries as veteran insurance behind Coleman.

Yet, even as multiple centers were traded across the league in the hours leading up to final roster cutdowns, Washington chose to stand pat.

The stakes: Protecting Jayden Daniels and executing David Blough's scheme

The consequences of this uneven roster construction could turn out to be a big deal when the regular season starts. Franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels must be kept clean to survive and thrive in his key 3 rd NFL season. Furthermore, newly promoted offensive coordinator David Blough —who is stepping into a major play-calling role for the first time—has promised a creative, high-speed offense designed to stress defenses. Neither Daniels' health, nor Blough's playbook, can thrive if the offensive line can't hold up against quality defensive talent.

This idea is scary when looking at the Commanders schedule . In the first half of the upcoming season alone, Washington must face some of the most destructive defensive lines and interior pass rushers in the NFL. The Commanders will have to match up against the division-rival Philadelphia Eagles' bruising front, a re-made Cowboys defensive unit under new DC Christian Parker, the Seahawks Super Bowl-caliber defense, and a Houston Texans defense boasting an elite edge-and-interior combination.

If a majority of the fan base is losing sleep as kickoff approaches, it's not for nothing. The front office has upgraded the defense from front to back and added weapons for the offense led by Jayden Daniels, but it's hard to feel confident that the offensive line – especially without Laremy Tunsil or a battle-tested center – will be up to the task.

With all that said, the Commanders have not yet taken a single regular season snap. Everything is still in front of them, and, in many ways, the team appears deeper and stronger than the 2024 group that played in the NFC Championship game. Joe Whitt has been replaced at DC by Daronte Jones – known for his teaching skill and and history with an aggressively attacking scheme. The DL, pass rushers and linebacking groups have all had major infusions of talent this offseason, and the secondary may benefit from the improved coaching and scheme that Jones is expected to bring to Washington.

Offensively, this may be the deepest and most talented group of wide receivers to play in Washington in at least a decade. A similar claim might be made about the tight end room, especially with respect to blocking ability. The running back group, while unheralded and without marquee name recognition, offers a mix of skills and styles that should be able to continue to produce the strong rushing metrics the Commanders put up under Dan Quinn in 2024 & 2025.

Most of all, every Commanders fan should know about the magical play of Jayden Daniels. It may not have been on display much in 2025, but we all remember what he was able to do in his rookie year when he was mostly healthy and playing behind an offensive line that was not really any better than the one he will rely on vs the Eagles next week. JD5's unique abilities, if he can avoid the kind of injuries that plagued him a year ago, erase a lot of mistakes and lift the play of every offensive player on the field with him. With Jayden Daniels, the Commanders go into every game with a chance to win.

The Commanders will open their 2026 NFL regular season on the road as underdogs against their division rivals.

articles.title: Rams Are Testing the Limits of Sleep Science Before Australia Game
articles.summary: The 49ers are already there, while the Rams have yet to leave.
articles.body:
When the Rams and 49ers play next week in Australia on the second day of the NFL season, their game plans will be dissected and debated. Their travel plans will be scrutinized as well.

The NFL is continuing to push the logistical boundaries of its bid to expand its international appeal with this Thursday-night game, played Friday morning in Melbourne.

"This is new," Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's EVP of club business, major events, and international, said in a video news conference this week. "You learn things every year. This is further than we've gone for a regular season game. But we feel really confident in the plan and the work we've done over many, many months working with the teams and our partners on the ground there in Melbourne."

The teams have taken wildly differing approaches to traversing the globe and trying to promote peak on-field performance.

The 49ers made their roughly 8,000-mile, 16-hour flight this week and already are in Australia, giving their players and coaches about a week to acclimate to the time zone, which is currently 17 hours ahead of California. The Rams have remained in Los Angeles to sleep in their own beds and practice at their own training facility for as long as possible before traveling next week; they are expected to arrive in Melbourne about 24 hours ahead of the game.

Dr. Jamie Zeitzer, a Stanford research professor who specializes in sleep medicine, said there are potential risks and benefits with each approach.

If the Rams' attempt is to have their players essentially operate on California time even while in Australia for their comparatively short stay there, Zeitzer told Front Office Sports , "that's kind of difficult to do, even if it's just for a day or two."

The circumstances must be very controlled.

"The main thing that you want to do is avoid light during the nighttime in California. So whenever it's night in California, you want to avoid light when you're in Australia, if you want to stay on California time," Zeitzer said. "My guess is they have the financial resources to do that. They're probably going to have a hotel where it's going to have blackout shades in the room and they can have their meetings in darkened ballrooms if necessary and have private chefs cooking for them breakfast, lunch, and dinner when they're expecting to have it in California, not necessarily the time in Australia."

The other issue with traveling so close to game time, he said, is the lingering effect of such a lengthy flight. Their travel accommodations will be top-notch, but "there are still negative consequences of being in a plane for that long in terms of your physical fitness," he said. "I do think they are risking that aspect of it. Even though it's nicer, it's [still] harder to sleep. And so are they going to be a bit sleep deprived from that plane ride? Is their circulation going to be as good? I think there is a risk there."

As for the 49ers, they might get close to acclimating by being in Australia for a week—but Zeitzer said even they probably won't fully adapt, either.

The kickoff time—10:35 a.m. Melbourne time Friday, which is 8:35 p.m. ET Thursday—will also test both teams' sleep strategies. There are two factors at work, Zeitzer said.

"One is the psychological aspect—like, 'I don't exercise at 10 o'clock in the morning.' But the other is the biological one. If you can spend the previous week basically training your body into expecting to need exercise at that time of day, then in theory it's going to be O.K. But, again, it's definitely a risk," he said.

In many cases when athletes compete in elite competition in a different time zone, they'll arrive far earlier than even the 49ers have for this game. "Usually when people do this—and they'll do it all the time for the Olympics—wealthier countries like the U.S. will send athletes like a month in advance to adapt. And you can basically try to time your exercise or your training to line up with when you're going to be expected to perform in a game," Zeitzer said.

If he'd had to choose, he would have picked the 49ers' approach.

Going any later, "there's pretty significant risk in taking a flight that long of having your sleep be pretty disrupted on that kind of flight and not having enough recovery time once you land … Going down and adapting, I think, is going to be better," he said. "I think there's a better chance of having optimal physical performance there."

The Rams, the widely acclaimed Super Bowl favorite entering the season, took a similar short-lead approach last season to a game in London. They remained in Baltimore following an October game against the Ravens the weekend ahead of their London trip, and practiced at Oriole Park at Camden Yards. They got to London similarly "late" and beat the Jaguars handily, 35–7.

"We felt like staying in our rhythm and routine and then traveling when we do… the thinking in its simplest form is what do we deem [is] the best for our football players and for them to try to be at their best," coach Sean McVay said in a news conference Friday. "There's different approaches and theories. But I do have a lot of trust in our group. And we'll see. Hopefully it works out. And I know that we've got a bunch of guys that I think will feel good about the plan."

The Rams are 3–0 under McVay in international games. He said he accepts the proposition that the Rams' travel approach will be subject to potential criticism if they lose to the 49ers.

Although arriving earlier can, on the surface, have fewer risks, "is there a right and a wrong?" Zeitzer asks. "I think it really has to do with how well you can control the behavior of grown men in this case."

articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are not a team many expect to be a major player in the 2026 NFL season — until proven otherwise. They have won just eight games in the last two seasons, and in both campaigns, finished last in the AFC North Division.

The quarterback situation of Cleveland, for one, does not exude much confidence among fans. Deshaun Watson has been given the keys to the offense on the field after winning a battle in the offseason for the starting quarterback role over Shedeur Sanders, and who knows how good the former Clemson Tigers quarterback can be in 2026.

In any case, the Browns are moving on with Watson, and his connection with his weapons downfield will be a major point of interest. Speaking of which, the Browns have an intriguing rookie in their wide receiving room, who could eventually become a difference-maker for Cleveland's attack .

Browns Rookie WR Has Intriguing Potential to Win Major NFL Award According to ESPN

First-year wideout KC Concepcion was selected 24th overall in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft, with the Browns seemingly believing in his potential to be a big contributor down the road for their offense.

Over at the Worldwide Leader in Sports, Concepcion is viewed as a sleeper to win the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Award.

Concepcion is a sleeper candidate to win OROY because of the multiple ways he could shine as a rookie. He not only has inside-out versatility in new coach Todd Monken's offense, but he's also a dynamic returner who can create positive plays on special teams. In Year 1 with Monken, playmakers outside of TE Harold Fannin Jr. are still unknown. Concepcion could quickly climb the ranks of reliable options and prove to be one of the more explosive young players in the NFL.

Concepcion will be given ample chance by Cleveland to show what he can bring to the table, especially in the early goings of the season, as he's expected to start alongside Jerry Jeudy and Denzel Boston, who was drafted a round later after Concepcion.

In his lone season with the Texas A&M Aggies in 2025, Concepcion racked up 919 receiving yards and nine touchdowns (most in the ACC) on 61 receptions through 13 games.
